% This file is not a live-book input and makes no novelty or priority claim.

Let \(B\) be a nonempty set.  Write \(X_B\) for the set obtained from
\(B\times[-\infty,0]\) by identifying all the points \((b,0)\) to one
point \(\eta\), and write
\[
                    p_b(t)=[(b,t)]\in X_B .
\]
We give \(X_B\) the topology of Chambert--Loir--Ducros,
Section~6.7.3: a subset \(V\subseteq X_B\) is open if and only if every
\[
 V_b=\{t\in[-\infty,0]:p_b(t)\in V\}
\]
is open in the order topology and, when \(\eta\in V\), the set of
\(b\in B\) for which \(V_b\ne[-\infty,0]\) is finite.  Thus this is not
the quotient topology when \(B\) is infinite.

A standard open neighbourhood of \(\eta\) is specified by a finite set
\(A\subseteq B\) and numbers \(R_a>0\), \(a\in A\), and has branches
\begin{equation}
 U_b=[-\infty,0]\quad(b\notin A),
 \qquad
 U_a=(-R_a,0]\quad(a\in A).
 \label{eq:p071-star-standard-neighbourhood}
\end{equation}
Every neighbourhood of \(\eta\) contains a standard one.

We use the exact smooth structure of that example.  A real-valued
function \(f\) on a neighbourhood of \(\eta\) is smooth precisely when
each \(f_b=f\circ p_b\) is ordinarily smooth on the finite stratum,
is constant on a neighbourhood of \(-\infty\) whenever that endpoint is
in its domain, only finitely many branches fail to be both full and
constant, and
\begin{equation}
                         \sum_{b\in B} f_b'(0)=0 .
 \label{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance}
\end{equation}
The sum in \eqref{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance} is finite.  For such a
smooth function, positivity of
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''f\) is equivalent to \(f_b''\geq0\) on every
finite branch stratum.  Let
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\) be this sheaf of smooth psh functions,
let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\) be the smallest subsheaf of the sheaf
of \(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\) and is stable under pointwise decreasing
sequential limits, and let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) be the sheaf
of functions which are locally pointwise decreasing limits of sections
of \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\).

On a standard neighbourhood \(U\) as in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-standard-neighbourhood}, define
\(\mathscr J_B(U)\) as follows.  A function
\(u:U\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) belongs to \(\mathscr J_B(U)\) if:
\begin{enumerate}
\item every branch function \(u_b=u\circ p_b\) is extended-real convex
  on finite subintervals of its domain, and, for each full branch,
  \begin{equation}
   u_b(-\infty)=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u_b(t)
             \quad\text{in }\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\};
   \label{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}
  \end{equation}
\item if \(c=u(\eta)\in\mathbf R\), then for every finite
  \(F\subseteq B\setminus A\), every \(r_b>0\), \(b\in F\), and every
  \(0<\rho_a<R_a\), \(a\in A\), one has
  \begin{equation}
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{c-u_b(-r_b)}{r_b}
       \leq
   \sum_{a\in A}\frac{u_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a}.
   \label{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance}
  \end{equation}
  The empty set \(F\) is allowed.
\end{enumerate}
On an arbitrary open subset of \(X_B\), define \(\mathscr J_B\) by these
conditions locally, using ordinary finite intervals away from \(\eta\),
the trace condition at an included endpoint \(-\infty\), and standard
neighbourhoods at \(\eta\).

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}
For the preceding CLD tropical star, one has an equality of sheaves
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}
   =\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}
   =\mathscr J_B.
 \label{eq:p071-star-first-stage-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, let \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}(V)\) and let
\(x\in V\).

If \(x=\eta\) and \(u(\eta)=-\infty\), there is one fixed open
neighbourhood \(W\subseteq V\) of \(\eta\) on which \(u\equiv-\infty\).

If \(x=\eta\) and \(c=u(\eta)\in\mathbf R\), there is one fixed standard
neighbourhood \(W\subseteq V\), with exceptional set \(A\), such that
all finite-stratum values of \(u|_W\) are real.  The endpoint derivatives
\begin{equation}
 d_i=D_-u_i(0)
     :=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{c-u_i(-r)}{r}
 \label{eq:p071-star-endpoint-derivatives}
\end{equation}
are real, \(d_b\geq0\) for \(b\notin A\), and
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{b\in B\setminus A}d_b+\sum_{a\in A}d_a\leq0.
 \label{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}
\end{equation}
The first sum is the supremum of its finite subsums.  In particular it
is finite, and \(u_b\not\equiv c\) on at most countably many full
branches.  There are smooth psh functions \(g_n\) on that one fixed
neighbourhood \(W\) such that
\begin{equation}
                  g_{n+1}\leq g_n,
                  \qquad
                  g_n\longrightarrow u|_W
                  \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-star-fixed-neighbourhood-approximation}
\end{equation}
At a point different from \(\eta\), the same fixed-neighbourhood
conclusion holds on an ordinary interval or on a constant-collar
neighbourhood of \(-\infty\).
\end{theorem}

% Exact isolated candidate statement for source-aware verification.
% This file makes no novelty or priority claim and is not a live-book input.

Let
\[
       \overline{\mathbf R}_{-}=\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\},
       \qquad S=[-\infty,R_0)\subseteq\overline{\mathbf R}_{-},
\]
where \(R_0\in\mathbf R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and give \(S\) its order
topology.  For an open subset \(W\subseteq S\), let
\(C^\infty_{-\infty}(W)\) be the real-valued functions \(f\) such that
\(f|_{W\cap\mathbf R}\) is smooth in the ordinary sense and, if
\(-\infty\in W\), there is \(a\in\mathbf R\) for which
\begin{equation}
 [-\infty,a)\subseteq W,
 \qquad f|_{[-\infty,a)}\ \text{is constant}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-collar-smoothness}
\end{equation}
Let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}(W)\) consist of the
\(f\in C^\infty_{-\infty}(W)\) such that
\begin{equation}
                         f''\geq0
                 \quad\text{on }W\cap\mathbf R.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-stage-zero}
\end{equation}
Let \(\operatorname{Psh}_S\) be the smallest subsheaf of the sheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions that contains
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}\) and is stable under pointwise decreasing
limits of sequences.  Let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,1}\) be the sheaf of
functions that are locally pointwise decreasing limits of sequences in
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}\).

For an open \(W\subseteq S\), define \(\mathscr J_{-\infty}(W)\) to be
the functions \(u:W\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) with the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The restriction of \(u\) to every finite real interval contained
in \(W\cap\mathbf R\) is extended-real convex: if
\(x,y\in W\cap\mathbf R\), \(0<\lambda<1\), and
\([x,y]\subseteq W\), then
\begin{equation}
 u\bigl((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y\bigr)
 \leq(1-\lambda)u(x)+\lambda u(y),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-extended-convexity}
\end{equation}
where every positive multiple of \(-\infty\) is \(-\infty\).
\item If \(-\infty\in W\) and \(W_{-\infty}\) is the connected
component of \(W\) containing \(-\infty\), then
\begin{equation}
 u(-\infty)
   =\lim_{t\to-\infty,\ t\in W_{-\infty}\cap\mathbf R}u(t)
       \quad\text{in }\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-endpoint-trace}
\end{equation}
In particular, the finite-side limit is not allowed to be \(+\infty\).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-cld-infinite-collar-endpoint}
With the preceding definitions, \(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\) is a sheaf and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Psh}_{S,1}
   =\operatorname{Psh}_S
   =\mathscr J_{-\infty}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-first-stage-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, suppose that \(-\infty\in W\) and
\(u\in\mathscr J_{-\infty}(W)\).  There is a fixed open neighbourhood
\(V=[-\infty,r)\subseteq W\) and functions
\(F_n\in\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}(V)\) such that
\begin{equation}
 F_{n+1}\leq F_n,
 \qquad F_n\longrightarrow u|_V
 \quad\text{pointwise on }V.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-fixed-domain-approximation}
\end{equation}
Each \(F_n\) is exactly constant on a neighbourhood of \(-\infty\).
If \(u(-\infty)\in\mathbf R\), then \(u\) is real-valued and continuous
on \(V\), and the convergence can be chosen uniform on \(V\).  The case
\(u(-\infty)=-\infty\) does not force \(u\) to be identically
\(-\infty\): for example, \(u(t)=t\) on the finite stratum, with
\(u(-\infty)=-\infty\), belongs to all three sheaves in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-first-stage-collapse}.

For the interval \(I=[-\infty,0)\) in
\cite[Example~6.7.2]{CLD25}, this is the constant-near-
\(-\infty\) smooth structure and
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-stage-zero} is the condition
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''f\geq0\).  Thus the theorem applies to the
one-dimensional G-tropical model of the trivially valued open unit disc
specified in that example.  It makes no assertion about stars, general
G-tropical spaces, or the global psh hierarchy outside this interval
model.
\end{theorem}

% Book-local finite-star polyhedral product theorem, 10 September 2026.
% It concerns only the explicitly defined ambient-induced generator sheaf.
% No priority claim is made.
\begin{theorem}[Finite ambient stars with polyhedral Euclidean directions]
\label{thm:p071-finite-star-polyhedral-collapse}
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let
\[
 S=\{0\}\cup\coprod_{i=1}^{m}(0,r_i)v_i\subset E,
 \qquad 1\leq m<\infty,
\]
where \(r_i>0\), \(v_i\ne0\), and the positive rays
\(\mathbf R_{>0}v_i\) are pairwise distinct.  Let \(P\) be a nonempty
convex polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real affine space; write
\(A:=\operatorname{Aff}(P)\).  Thus \(P\) may be unbounded or
zero-dimensional.  Put \(X:=S\times P\).
For an ordinary open \(W\subset X\), let \(\mathcal G_{X,0}(W)\) be the
real-valued functions which are locally restrictions of smooth ambient
functions on \(E\times A\) and for which, on every branch, the function
\[
 (t,y)\longmapsto g(tv_i,y)
\]
has positive-semidefinite full Hessian in the \((t,y)\) variables wherever
it is defined.  Let \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\) be the sheaf of local pointwise
decreasing limits of sequences in \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\), and let
\(\mathcal P_X\) be the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) and is closed under such limits.

Let \(\mathcal J_X(W)\) consist of the functions
\(u:W\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every branch \(i\), the function obtained by setting
      \(u_i(0,y):=u(0,y)\) and \(u_i(t,y):=u(tv_i,y)\) for \(t>0\)
      is extended-real jointly convex on every convex subset of
      \[
       \{(t,y)\in[0,r_i)\times P:(tv_i,y)\in W\};
      \]
\item whenever \((0,y_0)\in W\), finitely many points
      \((t_av_{i(a)},y_a)\in W\), and numbers \(\alpha_a\geq0\) satisfy
      \[
       \sum_a\alpha_a=1,
       \qquad
       \sum_a\alpha_at_av_{i(a)}=0,
       \qquad
       \sum_a\alpha_ay_a=y_0,
      \]
      and every segment from \((0,y_0)\) to a point with
      \(\alpha_a>0\) is contained in \(W\), then
      \[
       u(0,y_0)\leq\sum_a\alpha_a u(t_av_{i(a)},y_a).
       \tag{\(\mathrm J_{S\times P}\)}
      \]
      Terms with zero coefficient are omitted from the extended-real sum.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\mathcal J_X\) is a sheaf and
\[
                       \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal J_X.
\]
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on one fixed smaller
neighbourhood.  At a point of \(\{0\}\times P\), that neighbourhood may
be chosen to be the product of a smaller finite substar and a relatively
open polyhedral neighbourhood in \(P\).
\end{theorem}

% Quarantined P07.1 research candidate, 30 August 2026.
% This file is not a live-book input, has not received independent review,
% and has not been submitted to production Rethlas.  No novelty or priority
% claim is made.

Let \(Z\) be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen
subsets.  Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real affine space, let
\(P\subset E\) be a nonempty convex polyhedron, possibly unbounded and
possibly of dimension smaller than \(E\), and put
\(A=\operatorname{Aff}(P)\).  Set
\[
                              X=Z\times P .
\]

We use the following smooth psh generator sheaf on \(X\).  A real-valued
function \(f\) on an open subset of \(X\) is smooth if, locally at every
\((z,x)\), there are a clopen neighbourhood \(D\) of \(z\), an open
neighbourhood \(O\) of \(x\) in \(A\), and \(F\in C^\infty(O)\) such that
\[
                  f(z',x')=F(x')
       \quad\text{on }D\times(P\cap O).
\]
It is a smooth psh generator if the Hessian of \(F\) is positive
semidefinite at every point of \(P\cap O\).  Denote this sheaf by
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\), denote by
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\) its first local pointwise-decreasing-limit
stage, and denote by \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\) and is stable under local pointwise decreasing
limits of sequences.

Define \(\mathscr C_X\) by the following local condition.  A section \(u\)
belongs to \(\mathscr C_X\) near \((z_0,x_0)\) if there are
\begin{itemize}
\item a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\subset Z\) of \(z_0\);
\item a relatively open convex neighbourhood \(V\subset P\) of \(x_0\);
\item a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space \(Y\) and a continuous
  surjection \(q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y\); and
\item an upper semicontinuous function
  \(\bar u:Y\times V\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)
\end{itemize}
such that
\begin{equation}
 u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x),
 \qquad
 x\longmapsto\bar u(y,x)\text{ is extended-real convex for every }y\in Y.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-factorization}
\end{equation}
Here extended-real convexity uses no \(+\infty\) values and omits terms
with zero coefficient.

Then \(\mathscr C_X\) is a sheaf and
\begin{equation}
             \operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}
             =\operatorname{Psh}_X
             =\mathscr C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, if \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_X(W)\) and
\((z_0,x_0)\in W\), there are a compact clopen neighbourhood
\(C\ni z_0\), a relatively open polyhedral neighbourhood \(V\ni x_0\),
and smooth psh functions \(G_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times V)\)
such that
\begin{equation}
                         G_{k+1}\leq G_k,
             \qquad      G_k\longrightarrow u|_{C\times V}
             \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-fixed-domain}
\end{equation}

The same conclusion holds on every Hausdorff space equipped with a
generator sheaf which is locally identified, by generator-preserving
charts, with one of the preceding product models.  In particular it holds
on locally finite polyhedral manifolds with corners, with an arbitrary
locally compact clopen-base transverse parameter carrying only locally
constant affine directions.

For the standing \(K=\mathbf Q\), \(G=\mathbf R\) conventions of
Chambert--Loir--Ducros, a rational polyhedron \(P\) with its induced
affine tropical structure and \(Z\) with its locally constant affine
structure give the displayed generator sheaf through their product
construction.  The assertion is confined to this convex single-chamber
model.  It makes no claim for a nonconvex union of chambers, a branched
polyhedral complex, nonconstant affine directions on \(Z\), or an
arbitrary affine \(G\)-tropical space.  It therefore narrows but does not
retire P07.1.

% Book-local P07.1 candidate, 13 September 2026.
% This theorem combines the exact infinite CLD star with one convex
% polyhedral factor.  It makes no novelty or priority claim.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-infinite-star-polyhedral-collapse}
Let \(B\ne\varnothing\), let \(X_B\) be the exact
Chambert--Loir--Ducros star of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}, and let \(P\) be a
nonempty convex polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real affine space
\(L_P\).  Put
\[
                              X=X_B\times P.
\]

We use the following exact product generator sheaf.  On the product of an
ordinary interval in a branch with a relatively open convex subset of
\(P\), a real-valued generator is locally the restriction of an ambient
smooth function on \(\mathbf R\times L_P\) whose full Hessian in the branch
and polyhedral variables is positive semidefinite.  At a full endpoint
\(-\infty\), the generator is additionally constant in the branch variable
on a terminal collar, locally uniformly in the polyhedral variable.

At a node point, take a standard star neighbourhood \(U\), with finite
exceptional set \(A\subset B\) and exceptional collars
\((-R_a,0]\), and a relatively open convex set \(V\subset P\).  Write
\[
 g_b(t,y)=g(p_b(t),y),\qquad c_g(y)=g(\eta,y).
\]
A generator on \(U\times V\) is required to have jointly ambient-smooth
convex branch functions, one finite set \(K\subset B\setminus A\) such that
\begin{equation}
 g_b(t,y)=c_g(y)
 \quad
 \bigl(b\in B\setminus(A\cup K),\
       t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in V\bigr),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-finite-activity}
\end{equation}
and the exact balance law
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a\in A}\partial_tg_a(0,y)
   +\sum_{b\in K}\partial_tg_b(0,y)=0
 \qquad(y\in V).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-balance}
\end{equation}
On every full active branch, the terminal-collar condition is also imposed.
Let \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) be the sheaf defined by these local conditions,
let \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\) be its sheaf of local pointwise decreasing
sequential limits, and let \(\mathcal P_X\) be the smallest subsheaf of
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) and is closed under such limits.

Define a comparison sheaf \(\mathcal J_X\) as follows.  Its functions are
upper semicontinuous.  Every branch function \(u_b(t,y)\), with the node
value inserted at \(t=0\), is extended-real jointly convex on every ordinary
convex subset of its branch--polyhedral domain.  On a full branch,
\begin{equation}
 u_b(-\infty,y)=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u_b(t,y)
 \quad\text{in }\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-endpoint-trace}
\end{equation}
Near a node, require one standard product \(U\times V\) and one countable
set \(K\subset B\setminus A\) such that
\begin{equation}
 u_b(t,y)=c(y):=u(\eta,y)
 \quad
 \bigl(b\in B\setminus(A\cup K),\
       t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in V\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-countable-activity}
\end{equation}
Finally, let \(F\subset B\setminus A\) be finite, choose \(r_b>0\) for
\(b\in F\), choose \(0<\rho_a<R_a\) for \(a\in A\), and put
\[
 \Lambda=\sum_{b\in F}\frac1{r_b}
              +\sum_{a\in A}\frac1{\rho_a}.
\]
If \(\Lambda>0\), \(c(y_0)\in\mathbf R\), and
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda y_0=
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{y_b}{r_b}
      +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{y_a}{\rho_a},
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-barycentre}
\end{equation}
for points \(y_0,y_b,y_a\in V\), require the exact product junction
inequality
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda c(y_0)\leq
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{u_b(-r_b,y_b)}{r_b}
      +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{u_a(-\rho_a,y_a)}{\rho_a}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-junction}
\end{equation}
The case \(F=A=\varnothing\) is vacuous.  Membership in
\(\mathcal J_X\) means that every point has a neighbourhood on which these
conditions hold.

Then
\begin{equation}
                 \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal J_X.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of \(\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on one fixed smaller
neighbourhood.  At a node, this neighbourhood may be chosen as
\(U'\times V'\), with \(U'\) standard and \(V'\) relatively open and
convex in \(P\).  At a full endpoint it may be chosen as one fixed terminal
product neighbourhood.

The theorem permits an arbitrary branch set, all faces and corners of one
convex polyhedron, mixed branch--polyhedral Hessian terms, and the exact CLD
terminal collars.  It does not cover a separately convex generator sheaf,
an additional nonconstant Stone-affine direction, a non-CLD infinite star,
a nonconvex or branched chamber gluing, or a nonambient branch structure.
Consequently it narrows but does not retire P07.1.
\end{theorem}

% Book-local P07.1 theorem, 19 September 2026.
% This theorem combines the locally constant Stone parameter with the exact
% infinite CLD star and one active convex-polyhedral factor.  It makes no
% novelty or priority claim.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-stone-infinite-star-polyhedral-collapse}
Let $Z$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen
subsets, let $B\ne\varnothing$, let $X_B$ be the exact
Chambert--Loir--Ducros star of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}, and let $P$ be a
nonempty convex polyhedron in a finite-dimensional real affine space.
Put
\[
                         T=X_B\times P,
             \qquad      X=Z\times T.
\]
On $T$, retain the exact product generator sheaf $\mathcal G_{T,0}$ and
the comparison sheaf $\mathcal J_T$ of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-polyhedral-collapse}.

For an ordinary open $W\subset X$, let $\mathcal G_{X,0}(W)$ be the
real-valued functions which locally, after shrinking the $Z$-variable to
a clopen neighbourhood, are independent of that variable and belong to
$\mathcal G_{T,0}$ in the remaining variables.  Let $\mathcal P_{X,1}$
be the sheaf of local pointwise decreasing limits of sequences in
$\mathcal G_{X,0}$, and let $\mathcal P_X$ be the smallest subsheaf of
$\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}$-valued functions which contains
$\mathcal G_{X,0}$ and is closed under such limits.

Define a comparison sheaf $\mathcal C_X$ by the following local
condition.  A section $u$ belongs to $\mathcal C_X$ near
$(z_0,x_0)\in Z\times T$ if there are a compact clopen neighbourhood
$C\subset Z$ of $z_0$, a product neighbourhood $V_T\subset T$ of
$x_0$, a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space $Y$, a continuous
surjection $q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y$, and an upper semicontinuous function
\[
 \bar u:Y\times V_T\longrightarrow\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
 u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x),
 \qquad
 \bar u(\zeta,\cdot)\in\mathcal J_T(V_T)
 \quad(\zeta\in Y).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-factorization}
\end{equation}
Near a node point $(z_0,\eta,y_0)$, require in addition that
$V_T=U\times V$, where $U$ is a standard star neighbourhood with finite
exceptional set $A\subset B$ and $V$ is relatively open and convex in
$P$, and that there be one countable set $K\subset B\setminus A$,
independent of $\zeta$ and $y$, for which
\begin{equation}
 \bar u(\zeta,p_b(t),y)=\bar u(\zeta,\eta,y)
 \quad
 \bigl(\zeta\in Y,\ b\in B\setminus(A\cup K),\
       t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in V\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-common-activity}
\end{equation}

Then $\mathcal C_X$ is a sheaf and
\begin{equation}
                 \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of $\mathcal G_{X,0}$ on one fixed smaller
product neighbourhood.  At a node, that neighbourhood may be chosen as
$C\times U'\times V'$, with $C$ compact clopen, $U'$ standard, and
$V'$ relatively open and convex in $P$.

Thus a possibly nonmetrizable locally constant Stone parameter, an
arbitrarily large exact CLD branch set, and all affine directions, faces,
and corners of one convex polyhedron may occur simultaneously.  The
theorem still excludes nonconstant affine directions on the Stone factor,
non-CLD infinite stars, separately convex generators, nonambient branch
structures, and nonconvex or branched chamber gluings.  Consequently it
narrows but does not retire P07.1.
\end{theorem}

% Book-local P07.1 corollary, 20 September 2026.

% generator-preserving convex developments.  It makes no novelty or priority

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p071-stone-infinite-star-generator-convex-collapse}
Let $\Sigma$ be a possibly infinite Hausdorff face-to-face polyhedral
complex, not assumed locally finite, equipped with a sheaf
$\mathcal G_{\Sigma,0}$ of real-valued smooth psh generators.  Suppose that
every $p\in|\Sigma|$ has an open neighbourhood $U$, a finite-dimensional
real affine space $A$, a nonempty convex polyhedron $P\subset A$, a
relatively open convex subset $V\subset P$, and a homeomorphism
\[
                          \varphi:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V
\]
which carries the complete germ of $\mathcal G_{\Sigma,0}$ in both
directions to the single-chamber smooth psh generator sheaf on $V$.

Let $Z$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a basis of clopen subsets,
let $B\ne\varnothing$, and let $X_B$ be the exact
Chambert--Loir--Ducros star of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}.  Put
\[
                         X=Z\times X_B\times|\Sigma|
\]
and equip $X$ with the corresponding product generator sheaf
$\mathcal G_{X,0}$.  Let $\mathcal P_{X,1}$ be its first local decreasing
sequential stage and let $\mathcal P_X$ be its full generated psh sheaf.
Then
\begin{equation}
                         \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-star-generator-convex-collapse}
\end{equation}
Every germ has a pointwise decreasing approximation by members of
$\mathcal G_{X,0}$ on one fixed smaller product neighbourhood contained in
one displayed convex-development chart.  At a node of $X_B$, one countable
set of active full branches works simultaneously for the compact Stone
family and for every point of the smaller developed polyhedral
neighbourhood.

If $\mathcal C_X$ is defined chartwise by transporting the restriction of
the Stone-factorized comparison sheaf in
\Cref{thm:p071-stone-infinite-star-polyhedral-collapse}, then this
definition is independent of the chosen convex-development chart and
\[
                         \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal C_X.
\]
Thus arbitrary incidence, infinitely many cells through every
neighbourhood, and global chamber monodromy may coexist with a possibly
nonmetrizable locally constant Stone parameter and an arbitrarily large
exact CLD star.  The result does not cover a germ without a
generator-preserving convex development, in particular a branched or
singular lower link, nor does it cover nonconstant affine directions on the
Stone factor, non-CLD or nonambient stars, or separately convex generators.
Consequently it narrows but does not retire P07.1.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
We divide the proof into the comparison statement, the numerical
consequences at the centre, and the approximation construction.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Convex functions on a full branch.}
Let \(v:[-\infty,0]\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be extended-real
convex on the finite stratum and satisfy the exact trace condition at
\(-\infty\).  On the open ordinary interval \((-\infty,0)\), local
extended-real convexity gives the following alternative: \(v\) is
finite everywhere or \(v\equiv-\infty\).  Indeed, suppose that
\(v(x)=-\infty\) and \(v(y)\) is finite.  Choose \(z\) on the side of
\(y\) opposite to \(x\), so that \(y\) lies strictly between \(x\) and
\(z\).  The convexity inequality has right side \(-\infty\), regardless
of the value at \(z\), and contradicts the finiteness of \(v(y)\).
In the first case convexity also forces \(v(0)\) to be finite: if
\(v(0)=-\infty\), apply the same argument to a finite point and an
intermediate finite point.  In the second case \(v(0)\) may be finite
or \(-\infty\); the former possibility is the polar endpoint jump.

In every case \(v\) is nondecreasing in the extended order.  This is
automatic in the polar case.  In the finite-interior case, otherwise
there would be \(s<t\leq0\) for which
\[
                       q=\frac{v(t)-v(s)}{t-s}<0.
\]
For \(x<s\), monotonicity of the secant slopes of a convex function gives
\[
             \frac{v(s)-v(x)}{s-x}\leq q,
             \qquad
             v(x)\geq v(s)-q(s-x)\longrightarrow+\infty,
\]
contrary to the trace in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}, whose value is not \(+\infty\).
Consequently, if \(v(0)=c\in\mathbf R\), then \(v(t)\leq c\) for
every \(t<0\).  The quantities
\begin{equation}
                  p_v(r)=\frac{c-v(-r)}r
\label{eq:p071-star-secant-slope}
\end{equation}
are nonnegative and increase as \(r\downarrow0\).  Their limit is the
left derivative \(D_-v(0)\in[0,+\infty]\); in the polar case all of
them and the derivative are \(+\infty\).

The same elementary secant-slope argument, without the nonnegativity
conclusion, applies on an exceptional collar.  For every finite convex
function \(v\) on \([-R,0]\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{v(0)-v(-r)}r\leq D_-v(0)
 \qquad(0<r\leq R).
 \label{eq:p071-star-secant-below-derivative}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The comparison conditions form a sheaf.}
We first verify restriction at the centre.  Suppose that \(u\) satisfies
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on a standard neighbourhood
with exceptional set \(A\), and restrict to a smaller standard
neighbourhood whose exceptional set is \(A\cup E\), where \(E\) is
finite.  Apply \eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} before the
restriction to the union of a prescribed finite
\(F\subseteq B\setminus(A\cup E)\) and \(E\), choosing the desired
collar points on the branches in \(E\).  The same inequality with empty
full-branch set first shows that all sampled exceptional values are
finite, and its singleton instances show the same for the sampled
branches in \(E\).  Hence the following rearrangement is legitimate in
\(\mathbf R\).  Since
\[
 \frac{u_e(-\rho_e)-c}{\rho_e}
      =-\frac{c-u_e(-\rho_e)}{\rho_e},
\]
moving the terms indexed by \(E\) to the right gives precisely
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} for the restricted
neighbourhood.  Further shrinking of collars causes no difficulty.

For gluing, only the converse local-to-global implication at \(\eta\)
needs proof.  Let \(U\) be standard with exceptional set \(A\), and
suppose the comparison conditions hold on a smaller standard
\(W\subseteq U\) with exceptional set \(A\cup E\).  Fix the data in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(U\).  On each branch in
\(A\cup E\), choose a distance \(\sigma_i\) small enough that the
corresponding point lies in \(W\); take
\(\sigma_a\leq\rho_a\) for \(a\in A\) and, when \(e\in E\cap F\),
\(\sigma_e\leq r_e\).  The balance inequality on \(W\) with empty
full-branch set shows that every value sampled on the exceptional
branches \(A\cup E\) is finite: otherwise its right side would be
\(-\infty\).  Thus all the following rearrangements take place in
\(\mathbf R\).  By convexity, the secant slope
\eqref{eq:p071-star-secant-slope} increases when its distance decreases.
Therefore
\begin{align}
 \frac{u_a(-\sigma_a)-c}{\sigma_a}
   &\leq\frac{u_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a},
       &&a\in A,                                      \label{eq:p071-star-locality-a}\\
 \frac{u_e(-\sigma_e)-c}{\sigma_e}
   &\leq-\frac{c-u_e(-r_e)}{r_e},
       &&e\in E\cap F.                                \label{eq:p071-star-locality-e}
\end{align}
If \(e\in E\setminus F\), then \(e\) is a full branch of \(U\), so the
preceding branch argument gives \(u_e\leq c\), and its contribution on
the right side of the inequality on \(W\) is nonpositive.  Apply
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(W\) to \(F\setminus E\),
use \eqref{eq:p071-star-locality-a}--\eqref{eq:p071-star-locality-e},
discard the nonpositive terms indexed by \(E\setminus F\), and move the
terms indexed by \(E\cap F\) to the left.  The result is exactly
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(U\).

Branchwise convexity is local-to-global on an interval: on a compact
subinterval, take a finite interval cover on which convexity holds,
subdivide so that consecutive triples lie in members of the cover, and
use monotonicity of consecutive secant slopes.  The extended-real
open-stratum alternative from the first paragraph, together with the
possible polar endpoint jump, handles the value \(-\infty\).
The endpoint trace is local because any neighbourhood of \(-\infty\)
contains a complete terminal interval.  These observations, together
with the preceding restriction and gluing arguments, prove that
\(\mathscr J_B\) is a subsheaf.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Stability under decreasing limits.}
Let \(u_n\downarrow u\) on a standard neighbourhood.  Branchwise
extended-real convexity passes directly to the limit.  The exact trace
at a full endpoint also passes.  For completeness, put
\(c_n=u_n(-\infty)\) and \(c=u(-\infty)\).  Every function on a full
branch, including a polar one, is nondecreasing in the extended order,
so
\[
 c\leq \lim_{t\to-\infty}u(t).
\]
If \(c\in\mathbf R\), choose \(n\) with \(c_n<c+\varepsilon\), and then
take \(t\) sufficiently negative that
\(u(t)\leq u_n(t)<c+2\varepsilon\).  If \(c=-\infty\), the same argument
starts with \(c_n<M-1\) for an arbitrary \(M\in\mathbf R\).  This gives
the reverse trace inequality in both cases.

It remains to pass
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance}.  Suppose
\(u(\eta)=c\in\mathbf R\), and put \(c_n=u_n(\eta)\downarrow c\).
All full-branch terms on the left side for \(u_n\) are nonnegative.  No
sampled exceptional value can tend to \(-\infty\), since then the finite
right side would tend to \(-\infty\): every other exceptional value is
bounded above by its value for \(u_1\).  No sampled full-branch value can
tend to \(-\infty\), since then the left side would tend to \(+\infty\)
while the right side remains bounded above.  Thus every sampled limit is
finite, and termwise passage to the limit proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} for \(u\).  Hence
\(\mathscr J_B\) is stable under pointwise decreasing sequential limits.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Smooth psh functions satisfy the comparison conditions.}
Let \(f\) be smooth and psh on a standard neighbourhood, write
\(c=f(\eta)\), and set \(d_i=f_i'(0)\).  Branchwise positivity gives
convexity.  A full branch is constant near \(-\infty\), so \(d_b\geq0\)
for \(b\notin A\).  Smoothness gives
\[
             \sum_{b\notin A}d_b+\sum_{a\in A}d_a=0,
\]
with only finitely many nonzero terms.  By
\eqref{eq:p071-star-secant-below-derivative},
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{b\in F}\frac{c-f_b(-r_b)}{r_b}
 &\leq \sum_{b\notin A}d_b
  =-\sum_{a\in A}d_a\\
 &\leq \sum_{a\in A}\frac{f_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a}.
\end{align*}
The endpoint trace follows from the constant collar.  Thus every smooth
psh generator belongs to \(\mathscr J_B\).  The sheaf and limit properties
just proved, together with the minimal definition of
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\), give
\begin{equation}
                   \operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}
                         \subseteq\mathscr J_B.
 \label{eq:p071-star-psh-in-comparison}
\end{equation}
This argument applies at every transfinite stage without intersecting a
countable family of neighbourhoods.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite centre: slopes and countable activity.}
Let \(u\in\mathscr J_B(U)\) and suppose that \(c=u(\eta)\) is finite.
Shrink the exceptional collars so that every closed interval
\([-R_a,0]\) used below remains in the original domain.  Taking \(F\)
empty in \eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} shows that every
exceptional finite-stratum value is finite: one value \(-\infty\) would
make the right side \(-\infty\).  The same inequality with a singleton
full-branch set shows that every finite-stratum value on a full branch is
finite.  Hence all these branch functions are ordinarily continuous on
their open finite strata.

For an exceptional branch, \(d_a=D_-u_a(0)\) is bounded below by any
finite secant slope.  It cannot be \(+\infty\): keep the other
\(\rho_{a'}\) fixed and let \(\rho_a\downarrow0\) in the inequality with
\(F\) empty; the right side would tend to \(-\infty\).  Thus every
\(d_a\) is real.  A singleton full-branch inequality bounds
\(d_b\in[0,+\infty)\) from above.  Finiteness of these endpoint
derivatives rules out an upward jump at \(0\): for any fixed small
\(r_0>0\), convexity gives
\[
 \frac{c-u_i(-r_0)}{r_0}
   \leq \frac{c-u_i(-r)}r
   \leq d_i\qquad(0<r\leq r_0),
\]
so \(u_i(-r)\to c\).  Thus every branch function is continuous up to
\(0\).  Now let all \(r_b\downarrow0\) for a
fixed finite \(F\), and then let all \(\rho_a\downarrow0\).  We obtain
\begin{equation}
                   \sum_{b\in F}d_b
                       \leq-\sum_{a\in A}d_a.
 \label{eq:p071-star-finite-slope-bound}
\end{equation}
Taking the supremum over finite \(F\) proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}.  A family of nonnegative real numbers
with bounded finite subsums has countable positive support: for each
\(m\geq1\), only finitely many can be at least \(1/m\).  Finally, a full
branch with \(d_b=0\) is constant, since
\[
             0\leq\frac{c-u_b(-r)}r\leq d_b=0
\]
for every finite \(r>0\), and the endpoint trace then gives
\(u_b(-\infty)=c\).  Thus the nonconstant full branches form a countable
set.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite harmonic smoothing.}
We prove the approximation statement used in the final construction.
Consider a fixed standard neighbourhood and a real-valued continuous
function \(h\) on its closure such that only finitely many branches are
nonconstant, each branch function is convex, each full branch has the
exact finite endpoint trace, all branch values at \(\eta\) equal \(c_h\),
all endpoint derivatives \(D_-h_i(0)\) are finite real numbers, and
\begin{equation}
                        \sum_iD_-h_i(0)\leq0.
 \label{eq:p071-star-smoothing-input-balance}
\end{equation}
Only finitely many terms are nonzero, so this is an ordinary finite
sum.  We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\), there is a
smooth psh function \(H\) on the same open neighbourhood with
\begin{equation}
                         \lVert H-h\rVert_\infty<\delta.
 \label{eq:p071-star-finite-smoothing-error}
\end{equation}

On an exceptional closed collar, take a sufficiently fine finite
partition ending at \(0\) and form the chordal interpolant of \(h_i\).
On a full branch, first choose \(T_i<0\) so negative that replacing
\(h_i\) on \([-\infty,T_i]\) by the constant \(h_i(T_i)\) changes it by
less than an arbitrarily prescribed error; this is possible by the exact
endpoint trace and monotonicity.  Then use a fine chordal interpolant on
\([T_i,0]\).  The resulting piecewise-affine functions \(p_i\) are
convex and may be chosen within \(\delta/4\) of \(h_i\), are exactly
constant near every included
\(-\infty\), and have last slopes
\begin{equation}
                         s_i\leq D_-h_i(0).
 \label{eq:p071-star-chord-slope}
\end{equation}

We spell out a simultaneous smoothing which preserves both terminal
pieces exactly.  For every \(N\geq2\), choose a nonnegative product
mollifier \(\rho_N\in C^\infty_c((-1,1)^N)\), even in each variable and
of integral one, and set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal M_\tau(x_1,\ldots,x_N)
   =\int_{\mathbf R^N}
      \max_{1\leq j\leq N}(x_j+\tau y_j)\rho_N(y)\,\mathrm dy .
 \label{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum}
\end{equation}
This is the convolution of the maximum with a smooth compactly supported
kernel.  It is smooth, convex, nondecreasing in each variable, and
\[
 \left|\mathcal M_\tau(x)-\max_jx_j\right|\leq\tau.
\]
If, for some \(k\), \(x_k>x_j+2\tau\) for all \(j\ne k\), then the same
coordinate realizes the maximum throughout the support of \(\rho_N\).
Evenness gives \(\int y_k\rho_N(y)\,\mathrm dy=0\), and hence
\begin{equation}
                    \mathcal M_\tau(x)=x_k .
 \label{eq:p071-star-exact-dominance}
\end{equation}

Write a nonaffine \(p_i\) as the maximum of the affine extensions
\(\ell_{i1},\ldots,\ell_{iN_i}\) of its pieces.  Consecutive identical
pieces are first merged.  The last affine piece then strictly dominates
all the others at \(0\), and hence by a fixed positive margin on a
collar of \(0\).  On a full branch, its first, constant affine piece
strictly dominates all the others sufficiently far to the left.  Indeed,
after the merging, every other piece has positive slope there.  Choose
\(\tau>0\) smaller than half all these finitely many dominance margins
and also smaller than \(\delta/4\), and define
\[
 k_i(t)=\mathcal M_\tau
       \bigl(\ell_{i1}(t),\ldots,\ell_{iN_i}(t)\bigr).
\]
For an affine \(p_i\), simply take \(k_i=p_i\).  Convexity and coordinate
monotonicity of \(\mathcal M_\tau\) show that every \(k_i\) is smooth
and convex.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-dominance} show, respectively, that
\[
 \lVert k_i-h_i\rVert_\infty<\delta/2,
 \qquad k_i(0)=c_h,\qquad k_i'(0)=s_i,
\]
and that \(k_i\) is exactly constant on a collar of every included full
endpoint.  Put
\[
                         m=-\sum_i s_i\geq0,
\]
where nonnegativity follows from
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smoothing-input-balance} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-chord-slope}.

Choose one branch.  On a sufficiently short collar \([-\ell,0]\), take
a smooth function \(\beta\) whose derivative increases from \(0\) to
\(m\), is identically \(0\) to the left of that collar, and is identically
\(m\) near \(0\), normalized by \(\beta(0)=0\).  Explicitly, for a smooth
nondecreasing cutoff \(\chi\) which is \(0\) near \(0\) and \(1\) near
\(1\), one may prescribe
\[
 \beta'(t)=m\chi\!\left(\frac{t+\ell}{\ell}\right)
      \quad(-\ell\leq t\leq0),
 \qquad
 \beta(t)=-\int_t^0\beta'(s)\,\mathrm ds,
\]
and extend \(\beta\) constantly to the left.  Then
\(\beta''\geq0\), \(\beta'(0)=m\), and
\(-m\ell\leq\beta\leq0\).  Add \(\beta\) to the smoothed function on
the chosen branch, leaving all other branches unchanged and every
inactive branch equal to \(c_h\).  By choosing \(\ell\) sufficiently
small, the additional error is less than \(\delta/2\).  The endpoint
derivatives now sum to zero exactly.  The explicit CLD description in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance} shows that the glued function \(H\)
is smooth, including at \(\eta\); branchwise convexity gives
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''H\geq0\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-smoothing-error}.  Notice that the amplitude
of the derivative repair tends to zero with \(\ell\), even when \(m\)
is large.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{A decreasing approximation on one fixed neighbourhood.}
Return to a finite-centre \(u\in\mathscr J_B(U)\), after the preceding
shrinking.  Enumerate the nonconstant full branches as
\(C=\{b_1,b_2,\ldots\}\), stopping if \(C\) is finite.  For \(n\geq1\),
define \(w_n\) by
\begin{align}
 w_{n,a}&=\max\{u_a,c-n\}, &&a\in A,                 \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-a}\\
 w_{n,b_j}&=\max\{u_{b_j},c-n\}, &&j\leq n,          \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-b}\\
 w_{n,b}&=c, &&b\notin A\cup\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}.     \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-inactive}
\end{align}
The maximum of a convex function and a constant is convex.  The exact
trace on a full branch shows that the truncated function is finite and
continuous at \(-\infty\); on an exceptional branch it is finite and
continuous on the chosen closed collar.  Thus \(w_n\) is a finite
continuous branchwise-convex function on the closed standard star, with
only finitely many active branches.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                        w_{n+1}\leq w_n,
                        \qquad w_n\longrightarrow u
                        \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-star-truncations-decrease}
\end{equation}
Since truncation is inactive on a sufficiently short collar of \(0\),
the endpoint derivatives of \(w_n\) are \(d_a\), \(a\in A\), and
\(d_{b_j}\), \(j\leq n\).  Therefore
\[
             \sum_{a\in A}d_a+\sum_{j\leq n}d_{b_j}\leq0
\]
by \eqref{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}.  Apply the finite harmonic
smoothing just proved to \(w_n+\varepsilon_n\), where
\[
                \varepsilon_n=2^{-n},
                \qquad \delta_n=2^{-(n+4)}.
\]
It gives a smooth psh \(g_n\) on the same fixed open neighbourhood with
\begin{equation}
                  \lVert g_n-(w_n+\varepsilon_n)\rVert_\infty
                         <\delta_n.
 \label{eq:p071-star-smoothing-diagonal-error}
\end{equation}
For every point of that neighbourhood,
\begin{align*}
 g_n-g_{n+1}
 &> (w_n-w_{n+1})+(\varepsilon_n-\varepsilon_{n+1})
            -\delta_n-\delta_{n+1}\\
 &\geq 2^{-(n+1)}-2^{-(n+4)}-2^{-(n+5)}>0.
\end{align*}
Thus \(g_n\) decreases on one fixed neighbourhood.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-star-truncations-decrease} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smoothing-diagonal-error} show pointwise convergence
to \(u\), including at every \(-\infty\)-endpoint.  This proves
\(\mathscr J_B\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) at a finite-centre
germ.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Centre value \(-\infty\) and the remaining points.}
Suppose \(u\in\mathscr J_B\) and \(u(\eta)=-\infty\).  On a full branch,
the exact trace and convexity make the branch function nondecreasing, so
every value is at most \(u(0)=-\infty\); hence the whole full branch is
identically \(-\infty\).  On an exceptional collar, convexity with the
endpoint value \(-\infty\) forces the function to be \(-\infty\) on a
smaller collar.  Since there are only finitely many exceptional branches,
one simultaneous shrinking makes \(u\equiv-\infty\).  The smooth psh
constants \(-n\) decrease to this germ.

At an interior point of a branch, local extended-real convexity gives
either the identically \(-\infty\) case or an ordinary finite convex
function.  On a smaller relatively compact interval, extend it to a
finite convex function on \(\mathbf R\) by affine supporting rays.  If
\(P_s\) denotes convolution with the centred Gaussian of variance
\(2s\), then \(P_su\) is smooth and convex.  The semigroup identity and
Jensen's inequality give
\[
               0<s'<s\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P_{s'}u\leq P_su,
\]
and \(P_su\to u\) locally uniformly as \(s\downarrow0\).  The sequence
\(P_{1/n}u\) therefore gives the required fixed-interval approximation.

For clarity, we also give the endpoint construction.  Let \(v\) be a
branch function on \([-\infty,R)\) satisfying
\eqref{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}.  The identically \(-\infty\) case
is handled by constants.  Otherwise \(v\) is finite, convex, and
nondecreasing on the finite stratum.  Choose
\[
                         r<R_1<R_2<R
\]
and extend \(v|_{(-\infty,R_1]}\) to a finite convex nondecreasing
function \(\bar v\) on \(\mathbf R\) by the affine ray of slope
\[
                  \frac{v(R_2)-v(R_1)}{R_2-R_1}
\]
to the right of \(R_1\).  All slopes of \(\bar v\) lie in a bounded
interval, so its Gaussian regularizations
\(A_s=P_s\bar v\) are finite, smooth, convex, and nondecreasing, satisfy
\(A_{s'}\leq A_s\) for \(s'<s\), and converge uniformly to \(\bar v\)
with an error bounded by a constant times \(\sqrt{s}\).

Fix the two-variable regularized maximum
\(\mathcal M_\tau\) from
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum} and put
\[
                         H_n(t)=\mathcal M_\tau(t,-n).
\]
Then \(H_n\) is smooth, convex, and nondecreasing, equals \(-n\) for
all sufficiently negative \(t\), equals \(t\) for every fixed finite
\(t\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\(H_{n+1}\leq H_n\).  On the fixed endpoint neighbourhood
\([-\infty,r)\), define
\[
 F_n(t)=A_{1/n}(H_n(t)),\qquad
 F_n(-\infty)=A_{1/n}(-n).
\]
Every \(F_n\) is smooth and convex and is exactly constant on a
neighbourhood of \(-\infty\).  Moreover,
\[
 F_{n+1}=A_{1/(n+1)}\circ H_{n+1}
      \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_{n+1}
      \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_n=F_n.
\]
At a finite point, eventual equality \(H_n(t)=t\) and the heat error
give \(F_n(t)\to v(t)\).  At \(-\infty\), the same error gives
\[
             F_n(-\infty)-v(-n)\longrightarrow0,
\]
while the exact trace gives
\(v(-n)\to v(-\infty)\) in
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\).  Thus \(F_n\downarrow v\) pointwise on
one fixed endpoint neighbourhood, including when
\(v(-\infty)=-\infty\).

We have proved
\(\mathscr J_B\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) at every point.
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-star-psh-in-comparison} and the tautological
inclusions
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\), this is
\eqref{eq:p071-star-first-stage-collapse} and all the additional
assertions of the theorem.
\end{proof}

interval \(I\subseteq\overline{\mathbf R}\) with a G-tropical affine
structure for which parlinear functions are constant near every endpoint
belonging to the interval.  On a connected domain meeting such an
endpoint, every affine function is constant.  Sections~6.1.1 and 6.1.6
of \cite{CLD25} make tropical charts affine and their scalar coordinate
functions affine.  Together with \cite[Definition~6.2.1]{CLD25}, this
gives exactly \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-collar-smoothness} near the endpoint
\(-\infty\); away from that endpoint one uses the ordinary real affine
coordinate.  Conversely, an ordinary smooth function on the finite
stratum that is exactly constant on a terminal tail is represented by
the constant chart on that tail and by the ordinary coordinate on
endpoint-free neighbourhoods.  On the finite stratum,
\[
 \mathrm d'\mathrm d''f
       =f''(t)\,\mathrm d't\wedge\mathrm d''t,
\]
and the form vanishes on the terminal tail.  Hence positivity is exactly
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-stage-zero}.  Definition~8.1.1 and
Lemma~8.1.4 of \cite{CLD25} give the generated sheaf and ordinal
filtration used in the statement.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Convexity and the endpoint trace.}
We first record two elementary consequences of the definition of
\(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\).  A locally extended-real convex function on a
connected ordinary interval is either finite everywhere or identically
\(-\infty\).  Indeed, the set where its value is \(-\infty\) is open:
if \(u(a)=-\infty\), express each nearby point as a strict convex
combination of \(a\) and a point on its other side.  The finite locus is
also open, since a finite value lying strictly between a nearby
\(-\infty\) value and a point on the other side would violate convexity.
The two loci are disjoint and cover a connected interval.

Suppose now that \(u\) is finite and convex on a tail
\((-\infty,b)\) and that
\begin{equation}
             c=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u(t)
                    \in\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-finite-side-limit}
\end{equation}
Then \(u\) is nondecreasing.  Otherwise there would be \(a<d<b\) with
\[
                 q=\frac{u(d)-u(a)}{d-a}<0.
\]
For every \(x<a\), monotonicity of secant slopes for a convex function
would give
\[
       \frac{u(a)-u(x)}{a-x}\leq q,
       \qquad
       u(x)\geq u(a)-q(a-x)\longrightarrow+\infty
                    \quad(x\to-\infty),
\]
contrary to \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-finite-side-limit}.  The same
nondecreasing conclusion is automatic when \(u\equiv-\infty\).

These observations also prove that \(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\) is a sheaf.
The ordinary convexity inequalities glue by the one-dimensional
local-to-global criterion.  Explicitly, on a compact interval take a
Lebesgue number for a finite cover by intervals of local convexity, choose
a partition whose consecutive triples lie in members of the cover, and
use the monotonicity of the resulting successive secant slopes.  The
dichotomy just proved handles extended-real values.  Finally, a member of
an open cover that contains \(-\infty\) contains a full terminal tail, so
its local equality \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-endpoint-trace} is already the
endpoint equality for the glued section.

The sheaf \(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\) is stable under pointwise decreasing
limits.  To see the only nonformal point, let \(u_j\downarrow u\) on an
endpoint component and put \(c_j=u_j(-\infty)\) and
\(c=u(-\infty)=\inf_jc_j\).  Every \(u_j\), and hence \(u\), is
nondecreasing, so
\begin{equation}
 c\leq L:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u(t).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-one-trace-inequality}
\end{equation}
If \(c\in\mathbf R\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) one can choose
\(j\) with \(c_j<c+\varepsilon\).  By the endpoint trace of \(u_j\), for
all sufficiently negative \(t\) one has
\(u(t)\leq u_j(t)<c+2\varepsilon\), so \(L\leq c\).  If
\(c=-\infty\), then, given \(M\in\mathbf R\), choose \(j\) with
\(c_j<M-1\) and then a sufficiently negative \(t\) so that
\(u(t)\leq u_j(t)<M\).  Monotonicity makes the same estimate valid farther
to the left, whence \(L=-\infty\).  Together with
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-one-trace-inequality}, this proves preservation of
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-endpoint-trace}.  Convexity passes directly to a
decreasing limit because no \(+\infty\) values occur.

Every member of \(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}\) lies in
\(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\): it is convex on the finite stratum, is constant
on a terminal tail, and has the required endpoint trace.  Since the latter
is a sheaf stable under decreasing limits, minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                 \operatorname{Psh}_S
                    \subseteq\mathscr J_{-\infty}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-generated-in-trace-class}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Heat regularization with an exact terminal collar.}
Let \(-\infty\in W\), let \(u\in\mathscr J_{-\infty}(W)\), and shrink
the endpoint component so that
\([-\infty,R)\subseteq W\) for some \(R\in\mathbf R\).  If
\(u\equiv-\infty\) on the finite stratum of this tail, then the endpoint
trace gives \(u(-\infty)=-\infty\), and the smooth psh constants \(-n\)
give \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-fixed-domain-approximation} on every smaller
fixed tail.

We may therefore suppose that \(u\) is finite and convex on
\((-\infty,R)\).  Put \(c=u(-\infty)\).  By
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-endpoint-trace} and the preceding argument, \(u\)
is nondecreasing.  Choose
\[
                       r<R_1<R_2<R
\]
and define
\[
              m=\frac{u(R_2)-u(R_1)}{R_2-R_1}\geq0.
\]
If \(c\in\mathbf R\), finite convexity gives continuity on
\((-\infty,R)\), while the trace equality gives continuity at the
endpoint \(-\infty\) in the order topology.  This proves the continuity
assertion in the statement.

Extend \(u\) to a finite function \(\bar u:\mathbf R\to\mathbf R\) by
\begin{equation}
 \bar u(t)=
 \begin{cases}
     u(t),&t\leq R_1,\\
     u(R_1)+m(t-R_1),&t\geq R_1.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-convex-extension}
\end{equation}
The monotonicity of secant slopes shows that this extension is convex and
nondecreasing.  Every one of its secant slopes belongs to \([0,m]\), so
\begin{equation}
              |\bar u(x)-\bar u(y)|\leq m|x-y|
                    \quad(x,y\in\mathbf R).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-global-lipschitz}
\end{equation}

For \(s>0\), set
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_s(y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi s}}
       \mathrm e^{-y^2/(4s)},
 \qquad
 A_s(t)=\int_{\mathbf R}\bar u(t-y)\gamma_s(y)\,\mathrm dy.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-heat-regularization}
\end{equation}
The linear-growth bound in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-global-lipschitz} makes the integral finite.
Every \(A_s\) is smooth, convex, and nondecreasing.  The Gaussian
semigroup identity and Jensen's inequality show that
\begin{equation}
             0<s'<s\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_{s'}\leq A_s.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-heat-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
Indeed, \(A_s=P_{s-s'}A_{s'}\), and averaging a convex function against
a centred probability measure can only increase it.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 0\leq A_s(t)-\bar u(t)
 \leq m\int_{\mathbf R}|y|\gamma_s(y)\,\mathrm dy
 =\frac{2m}{\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{s}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-heat-error}
\end{equation}

Choose a nonnegative even
\(\theta\in C^\infty_c((-1,1))\) of integral one.  For \(\eta>0\), put
\(\theta_\eta(s)=\eta^{-1}\theta(s/\eta)\) and
\begin{equation}
 M_\eta(a,b)=\int_{\mathbf R^2}
    \max\{a+s_1,b+s_2\}\theta_\eta(s_1)\theta_\eta(s_2)
       \,\mathrm ds_1\,\mathrm ds_2.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-exact-maximum}
\end{equation}
This is a smooth convex function, nondecreasing in each variable, and
\begin{align}
 M_\eta(a,b)&=a &&\text{if }a>b+2\eta,
 \notag\\
 M_\eta(a,b)&=b &&\text{if }b>a+2\eta,
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-exact-maximum-regions}\\
 \max\{a,b\}&\leq M_\eta(a,b)\leq\max\{a,b\}+\eta.
 \notag
\end{align}
Fix \(\eta>0\) small enough that \(r+3\eta<R_1\), and define, for
\(n\geq1\),
\begin{equation}
 H_n(t)=M_\eta(t,-n)\quad(t\in\mathbf R),
 \qquad H_n(-\infty)=-n.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-terminal-clamp}
\end{equation}
Then \(H_n\) is smooth, convex, and nondecreasing on the finite stratum,
is exactly equal to \(-n\) for \(t<-n-2\eta\), and is exactly equal to
\(t\) for \(t>-n+2\eta\).  Since \(M_\eta\) is nondecreasing in its
second variable,
\begin{equation}
                         H_{n+1}\leq H_n.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-clamp-monotonicity}
\end{equation}

On the fixed open tail \(V=[-\infty,r)\), set
\begin{equation}
 F_n(t)=A_{1/n}(H_n(t))\quad(t\in V\cap\mathbf R),
 \qquad
 F_n(-\infty)=A_{1/n}(-n).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-approximants}
\end{equation}
The function \(F_n\) is exactly constant on the endpoint collar
\(V\cap[-\infty,-n-2\eta)\).  On the finite stratum it is smooth and
\[
 F_n''
  =A_{1/n}''(H_n)(H_n')^2+A_{1/n}'(H_n)H_n''\geq0.
\]
Thus \(F_n\in\operatorname{Psh}_{S,0}(V)\).  By
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-heat-monotonicity},
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-clamp-monotonicity}, and monotonicity of
\(A_{1/n}\),
\begin{align}
 F_{n+1}
 &=A_{1/(n+1)}\circ H_{n+1}
 \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_{n+1}
 \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_n=F_n.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-approximants-decrease}
\end{align}

For every finite \(t<r\), one has \(H_n(t)=t\) for all sufficiently large
\(n\).  Equation \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-heat-error} therefore gives
\(F_n(t)\to u(t)\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the point \(-n\)
lies in \((-\infty,R_1]\), so \(\bar u(-n)=u(-n)\).  At the endpoint, the
same estimate then gives
\begin{equation}
 |F_n(-\infty)-u(-n)|
   =|A_{1/n}(-n)-\bar u(-n)|
   \leq\frac{2m}{\sqrt{\pi n}},
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-endpoint-convergence}
\end{equation}
while \(u(-n)\to c=u(-\infty)\) in
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\).  This proves pointwise convergence on
the fixed tail, including when \(c=-\infty\).

If \(c\in\mathbf R\), the convergence is uniform on \(V\).  Indeed, for
all large \(n\), \(\bar u=u\) on the range \(H_n(V)\).  When
\(t>-n+2\eta\), the clamp is the identity.  When
\(t\leq-n+2\eta\), the bounds in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-exact-maximum-regions} give
\[
                 t\leq H_n(t)\leq-n+3\eta,
\]
and monotonicity gives
\[
 0\leq u(H_n(t))-u(t)\leq u(-n+3\eta)-c.
\]
For finite \(t\), the inequalities \(H_n(t)\geq t\),
\(A_{1/n}\geq\bar u\), and monotonicity of \(\bar u\) also give
\(F_n(t)\geq u(t)\).  At the endpoint,
\[
 0\leq F_n(-\infty)-c
 \leq\frac{2m}{\sqrt{\pi n}}+u(-n)-c
 \leq\frac{2m}{\sqrt{\pi n}}+u(-n+3\eta)-c.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-heat-error}, these estimates yield
\[
 0\leq\sup_{t\in V}\bigl(F_n(t)-u(t)\bigr)
 \leq\frac{2m}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
       +u(-n+3\eta)-c\longrightarrow0.
\]

\medskip\noindent\emph{Interior points and conclusion.}
At an interior point, the extended-real dichotomy reduces matters either
to the constants \(-n\), or to a finite convex function on an ordinary
interval.  In the latter case, restrict to a compact subinterval and
extend the function to a finite convex function on \(\mathbf R\) by
affine supporting lines at its two endpoints.  Its heat regularizations
\(A_{1/n}\) are smooth and convex, decrease by
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-heat-monotonicity}, and converge to the original
function.  Thus every section of \(\mathscr J_{-\infty}\) belongs locally
to \(\operatorname{Psh}_{S,1}\).  Hence
\[
 \mathscr J_{-\infty}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{S,1}
 \subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_S.
\]
Combining this with
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-generated-in-trace-class} proves
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-first-stage-collapse} and all the stated
approximation assertions.  Finally, \(u(t)=t\), with endpoint value
\(-\infty\), satisfies the trace condition and is obtained explicitly
by the same construction.
\end{proof}

tuple.  An open member containing its node contains, for all sufficiently
small \(s>0\), the segments from \((0,y_0)\) to
\[

\]
The local junction inequality at these contracted points, followed by
branchwise convexity, gives the asserted inequality after cancelling
\((1-s)u(0,y_0)\) and dividing by \(s\).  The case
\(u(0,y_0)=-\infty\) is automatic.  Thus \(\mathcal J_X\) is a sheaf.
It is closed under pointwise decreasing limits, since both extended-real
convexity and every finite junction inequality pass to such a limit.
Every generator belongs to \(\mathcal J_X\): its ambient affine tangent at
\((0,y_0)\) is a minorant on every branch, and its weighted linear terms
cancel at the displayed barycentre.  Hence
\[
                         \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal J_X.

\]

It remains to prove the reverse inclusion at the first stage.  Away from
\(\{0\}\times P\), this is the one-point case of
\Cref{thm:p071-stone-polyhedral-collapse}, with a singleton clopen
parameter and a sufficiently small convex polyhedral normal-coordinate
interval.  We work at \((0,y_0)\), with \(u\in\mathcal J_X\) defined on
a product neighbourhood.  Choose numbers \(0<2T_i<r_i\), bounded open
polyhedra \(O_1,O_0\subset A\), and put
\[
 V=P\cap O_1,\qquad Q=P\cap\overline{O_0},
\]
so that \(y_0\in V\), \(\overline V^{\,P}\subset Q\), \(Q\) is a
compact convex polytope, and
\[
 D:=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,2T_i]v_i\Bigr)\times Q
\]
is contained in the original domain.  We first construct continuous finite
comparison majorants of \(u|_D\).  This is the step which treats every
polyhedral face and corner.

For a continuous real-valued function \(\phi\) on \(D\), define its
\emph{junction-convex envelope} \(C\phi\) as follows.  At a point
\(x=(tv_i,y)\) with \(t>0\), take the infimum of
\[
                   \sum_a\alpha_a\phi(s_av_{j(a)},y_a)
 \tag{\(\clubsuit\)}
\]
over all finite tuples in \(D\) satisfying
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_a\alpha_a&=1,
 &\sum_a\alpha_as_av_{j(a)}&=tv_i,\\
 \sum_a\alpha_ay_a&=y,
 &\sum_{j(a)=i}\alpha_as_a&\geq t.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_1\)}
\]
At a node \((0,y)\), use the same definition but omit the last inequality;
it is then independent of a branch label.  The singleton tuple shows that
\(C\phi\leq\phi\).

We record the three properties of this envelope needed below.  First,
\(C\phi\) satisfies the two comparison conditions on \(D\).  Indeed,
convex combinations of admissible tuples prove branchwise convexity, and
combining admissible tuples for a balanced node family proves the junction
inequality.  Second, it is the largest function satisfying those conditions
below \(\phi\).  To see this, let \(v\) satisfy them with \(v\leq\phi\),
and consider a tuple in
\((\clubsuit_1)\).  Put
\[
               \lambda=\sum_{j(a)=i}\alpha_as_a\geq t.
\]
For \(t>0\), retain the proportion \(t/\lambda\) of each branch-\(i\)
weight and call all remaining weights residual.  The retained weights have
normal moment \(tv_i\), while the residual weights have normal moment zero.
If the residual mass is nonzero, apply the junction inequality to its
Euclidean barycentre in \(Q\), and then apply branchwise convexity to that
node and the retained branch-\(i\) points.  This gives
\[
                  v(tv_i,y)\leq
                  \sum_a\alpha_av(s_av_{j(a)},y_a).
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_2\)}
\]
If the residual mass is zero, this is ordinary branchwise convexity.  At a
node, \((\clubsuit_2)\) is precisely the junction inequality.  Taking the
infimum proves \(v\leq C\phi\).

Third, \(C\phi\) is finite and continuous on \(D\).  For attainment and
lower semicontinuity, regard the tuples as probability measures on the
compact space \(D\).  Their Euclidean and normal moment constraints are
closed.  The extra branch-\(i\) moment is the integral of the continuous
function which equals \(s\) on branch \(i\), zero on the other branches,
and zero at the common node.  Compactness therefore supplies a minimizing
measure and shows lower semicontinuity under convergent target points; at a
node pass to one of the finitely many branch labels.  Carath\'eodory applied
also to the cost coordinate replaces every minimizing measure by a finite
one, as used in \((\clubsuit)\).  The function \(C\phi\) is finite and
convex on each compact branch prism \([0,2T_i]\times Q\).  A finite convex
function on a compact polytope is upper semicontinuous: triangulate near a
point with that point as a vertex and use the barycentric coefficient tending
to one.  Thus lower and upper semicontinuity give continuity on each branch,
and the common node values glue the finitely many branches continuously.

The restriction to \(D\) of every member of \(\mathcal J_X\) is upper
semicontinuous.  Indeed, \(\max\{u,-N\}\) is finite and satisfies the two
comparison conditions on \(D\): the maximum operation is convex and
nondecreasing, so Jensen's inequality preserves both defining conditions.
It is upper semicontinuous on each compact branch prism by the preceding
polyhedral argument, hence on \(D\); taking the decreasing infimum over
\(N\) proves the assertion for \(u\).

Fix a compatible metric \(d\) on \(D\).  The standard compact-metric
upper regularization
\[
 \phi_n(x):=\sup_{z\in D}
 \left(\max\{u(z),-n\}-n\,d(x,z)\right)
 \tag{\(\clubsuit_3\)}
\]
is finite, continuous, decreases to \(u\), and dominates \(u\).  For the
last assertion, an upper bound for \(u\) on \(D\) and upper
semicontinuity separate a small ball about the chosen point from its compact
complement; the penalty in \((\clubsuit_3)\) then forces convergence.  Set
\[
                              H_n:=C\phi_n.
\]
The preceding three properties give
\[
       u\leq H_n\leq\phi_n,\qquad H_{n+1}\leq H_n,\qquad H_n\downarrow u,

\]
and every \(H_n\) is finite, continuous, and satisfies the two comparison

We next give a uniform smooth majorant for one such continuous comparison

\(p\in A^*\) put
\[
 f_i(t,p)=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(H_i(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),
 \qquad
 f_0(p)=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(H(0,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr).
 \tag{\(\spadesuit\)}
\]
These are finite continuous scalar star profiles, convex in \(t\), with
common central value \(f_0(p)\).  The product junction inequality proves

normal tuple choose \(y_a\in Q\), put \(\bar y=\sum_a\alpha_ay_a\), and
write
\[
 \begin{split}
 f_0(p)
 &\leq H(0,\bar y)-p\mathbin\cdot\bar y\\
 &\leq\sum_a\alpha_a
      \bigl(H_{i(a)}(t_a,y_a)-p\mathbin\cdot y_a\bigr).
 \end{split}
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_1\)}
\]
Taking independent infima proves the claim.

 H_i(t,y)=\sup_{p\in A^*}

 H_i(t,y)\leq\widehat H_{\ell,i}(t,y)

\]

and having integral one, and set
\[
 M_{\delta,m}(x)=\int_{\mathbf R^m}\max_k(x_k+z_k)
     \prod_{k=1}^m\delta^{-1}\theta(z_k/\delta)\,\mathrm{d}z.
\]
This function is smooth, convex, and nondecreasing in every coordinate.
The symmetry and support of the kernel give
\[
 \max_kx_k\leq M_{\delta,m}(x)\leq\max_kx_k+\delta,
\]
and $M_{\delta,m}(x)=x_a$ when
$x_a>x_k+2\delta$ for every $k\ne a$: throughout the convolution
support the same coordinate realizes the maximum, and all first moments of
the kernel vanish.

Choose $0<C<\varepsilon/2$ and $0<\delta<C/2$ with
$C+\delta<\varepsilon$.  On branch $i$, apply the preceding
regularized maximum to $c+C+\xi_j(tv_i)$ and to the affine extensions of
the pieces of $h_i$.  By $(\spadesuit_8)$, the resulting $g_j$ satisfies
\[
                  h_\ell(\cdot,p_j)\leq g_j
                  \leq h_\ell(\cdot,p_j)+\varepsilon.
 \tag{$\spadesuit_9$}
\]
At the node the first input exceeds every other input by at least $C$,
so on an initial interval of every branch the regularized maximum equals
the single ambient affine function $c+C+\xi_j$.  Since the star and the
set of profiles are finite, the corresponding node collars may be chosen
simultaneously.  Thus every $g_j$ is smooth ambient-induced on the fixed
smaller substar and branchwise convex there.
The functions \(g_j(tv_i)+p_j\mathbin\cdot y\) are ambient-smooth and
jointly convex in \((t,y)\).  Taking their convex coordinatewise
nondecreasing regularized maximum, with error \(\varepsilon\), and adding
one further \(\varepsilon\), gives a function
\(w\in\mathcal G_{X,0}\) on the fixed product
\[
 V_X:=\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\coprod_i(0,\rho_i)v_i\Bigr)\times V,
 \qquad 0<\rho_i<T_i,
\]
such that
\[
                         H\leq w\leq H+4\varepsilon
 \quad\text{on }V_X.
 \tag{\(\spadesuit_{10}\)}
\]
The affine collar at the common node exists simultaneously because only
finitely many scalar profiles occur; it may depend on \(n\), while the
displayed product neighbourhood does not.  All functions are ambient smooth
in the \(A\)-variables, so this step also applies on every face of \(P\).

Apply this construction to \(H_n\) with a summable positive sequence
\((\varepsilon_n)\), producing \(w_n\) on the one fixed \(V_X\).  Put
\[
 d_n:=4\sum_{k>n}\varepsilon_k,
 \qquad G_n:=w_n+d_n.
\]
Equations \((\clubsuit_4)\) and \((\spadesuit_{10})\) give
\[
 G_{n+1}\leq H_{n+1}+4\varepsilon_{n+1}+d_{n+1}
 \leq H_n+d_n\leq G_n.
\]
Since \(H_n\downarrow u\) and \(4\varepsilon_n+d_n\to0\), the sequence
\(G_n\) decreases pointwise to \(u\) on \(V_X\).  Thus
\(\mathcal J_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}\).  Combining this with
\((\dagger)\) and \(\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X\) proves the
theorem.
\end{proof}
