\begin{proof}
We first isolate three elementary points which will be used twice.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Local extended-real convexity on a convex set.}
Let \(H\) be a convex subset of a finite-dimensional affine space and let
\(v:H\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be locally extended-real convex.  Then
\(v\) is extended-real convex on \(H\).  It is enough to restrict to a
segment and prove the assertion on an interval \(I\).  On
\(I^\circ\), both
\[
 \{t:v(t)\in\mathbf R\}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \{t:v(t)=-\infty\}
\]
are open.  For the first set, if a finite point had arbitrarily close
\(-\infty\) points, write the finite point as a strict convex combination
of one of them and a point on its other side, inside one interval of local
convexity.  For the second set, if \(v(t)=-\infty\), then every sufficiently
nearby \(s\) lies strictly between \(t\) and another point of the same
local convexity interval; the convexity inequality forces
\(v(s)=-\infty\).  Connectedness of \(I^\circ\) shows that \(v\) is either
finite throughout \(I^\circ\) or identically \(-\infty\) there.

In the first case an included endpoint cannot have value \(-\infty\):
local convexity there would propagate \(-\infty\) to a one-sided interior
collar.  Thus \(v\) is finite on \(I\), and the usual subdivision argument
applies: on a partition fine enough that each pair of consecutive
subintervals lies in a local convexity interval, the successive secant
slopes are nondecreasing.  Summing the slope inequalities proves global
convexity.  In the second case every convexity inequality at a point of
\(I^\circ\) has left side \(-\infty\), while the endpoint cases are
tautological.  This proves the assertion, including possible finite values
at the two endpoints of an otherwise polar segment.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Continuous convexification on a polytope.}
Let \(K\) be a compact convex polytope in a \(d\)-dimensional affine space
and let \(\phi:K\to\mathbf R\) be continuous.  Put
\begin{equation}
 (\operatorname{co}_K\phi)(x)
 =
 \inf\left\{
       \sum_i\alpha_i\phi(x_i):
       \alpha_i\geq0,\ \sum_i\alpha_i=1,\
       \sum_i\alpha_i x_i=x
      \right\}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope}
\end{equation}
This is the largest convex function on \(K\) bounded above by \(\phi\).
It is finite and continuous.

For completeness, every combination in
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope} can be replaced, without
increasing its value, by one with at most \(d+1\) nonzero coefficients.
Indeed, if there are more, affine dependence gives numbers \(\beta_i\),
not all zero, with
\[
             \sum_i\beta_i=0,\qquad \sum_i\beta_i x_i=0.
\]
Move the weights along one of the two directions
\(\alpha_i+t\beta_i\) for which the objective does not increase, until a
coefficient becomes zero, and iterate.  It follows that the infimum is
attained on a compact parameter space.  If \(x_j\to x\), choose minimizing
representations for \(x_j\) and pass to a convergent subsequence.  The
limiting representation is admissible for \(x\), which proves
\[
 \operatorname{co}_K\phi(x)
 \leq\liminf_j\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x_j).
\]
Thus the envelope is lower semicontinuous.  Convexity follows by combining
two admissible representations.

It remains only to check upper semicontinuity at the boundary of \(K\).
Fix \(x\in K\).  A finite triangulation of \(K\) may be refined so that
\(x\) is a vertex and the closed star of \(x\) is a neighbourhood of
\(x\) in \(K\).  If \(x_j\to x\), pass through the finitely many simplices
of that star.  In a simplex containing \(x\), the barycentric coefficient
of \(x\) tends to one.  Convexity bounds the envelope at \(x_j\) by the
same barycentric combination of its values at \(x\) and at the other
vertices.  The latter values are finite, hence
\[
 \limsup_j\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x_j)
 \leq\operatorname{co}_K\phi(x).
\]
This proves continuity.  Notice that polyhedrality is used exactly in
this boundary argument.

The convexification operation is nonexpanding in the uniform norm:
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\operatorname{co}_K\phi-\operatorname{co}_K\psi\right\|_K
 \leq \|\phi-\psi\|_K .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-envelope-nonexpanding}
\end{equation}
This follows immediately by applying
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-convex-envelope} to the same barycentric
representations in both directions.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Smooth convex majorants on one fixed polytope.}
If \(a:K\to\mathbf R\) is continuous and convex, then for every
\(\varepsilon>0\) there is a smooth convex function \(g\) on the whole
affine span of \(K\) such that
\begin{equation}
                       a\leq g\leq a+\varepsilon
                       \qquad\text{on }K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}
\end{equation}
To see this, extend \(a\) by \(+\infty\) off \(K\).  The resulting function
is proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous.  Strict separation of its
closed epigraph from the point \((x,a(x)-\delta)\) gives, for every
\(x\in K\) and \(\delta>0\), an affine function \(\ell_x\) such that
\[
                         \ell_x\leq a\text{ on }K,
              \qquad     \ell_x(x)>a(x)-\delta .
\]
The sets on which \(\ell_x>a-\delta\) form an open cover of \(K\).
After taking a finite subcover and putting
\[
                              p=\max_j\ell_{x_j},
\]
we obtain a globally defined convex piecewise-affine function satisfying
\[
                              a-\delta<p\leq a
                              \qquad\text{on }K.
\]
Choose a nonnegative smooth compactly supported probability kernel
\(\rho\) of barycentre zero.  The function \(p\) is globally Lipschitz;
if \(L\) is a Lipschitz constant, then
\[
                  p\leq p*\rho_r\leq p+Lr .
\]
The first inequality is Jensen's inequality.  Taking
\(\delta=\varepsilon/3\), choosing \(r\) with
\(Lr<\varepsilon/3\), and setting
\[
                              g=p*\rho_r+\delta
\]
proves \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}.  If \(L=0\), any
sufficiently small \(r\) works.  This argument is uniform for any finite
family of continuous convex functions by choosing the smoothing radii
separately.

\medskip\noindent
We now turn to the comparison sheaf.  Its defining condition is local, so
it is a sheaf.  Every smooth psh generator belongs to
\(\mathscr C_X\): after a clopen shrinking it is independent of \(z\);
take \(Y\) to be a point.  Positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian implies
convexity on each convex relative neighbourhood in \(P\).

We prove that \(\mathscr C_X\) is stable under decreasing sequential
limits.  Let \(u_n\downarrow u\) on an open subset \(W\subset X\), with
\(u_n\in\mathscr C_X(W)\), and fix \((z_0,x_0)\in W\).  Local compactness
and the clopen basis give a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\) of \(z_0\).
Choose bounded open polyhedra \(O_1,O_0\subset A\), both containing
\(x_0\), such that
\[
 \overline{O_1}\subset O_0,\qquad
 C\times\bigl(P\cap\overline{O_0}\bigr)\subset W.
\]
After making the polyhedra smaller if necessary, we may and do suppose that
\[
       V=P\cap O_1\quad\text{is convex},\qquad
       K=P\cap\overline{O_0}\quad\text{is a compact convex polytope}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-compact-core}
\]

For each fixed \(n\), compactness gives a finite product cover of
\(C\times K\) by sets
\begin{equation}
                           C_{n,a}\times V_{n,a},
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-local-factor-cover}
\end{equation}
where \(C_{n,a}\) is compact clopen in \(C\), \(V_{n,a}\) is relatively
open in \(P\), and on this product \(u_n\) factors through a continuous
surjection
\[
                  q_{n,a}:C_{n,a}\twoheadrightarrow Y_{n,a}
\]
onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space.  Choose a countable
clopen base \(\mathcal D_{n,a}\) of each \(Y_{n,a}\).  Let
\(\mathcal B\) be the Boolean subalgebra of the clopen subsets of \(C\)
generated by all \(C_{n,a}\) and all
\[
                     q_{n,a}^{-1}(D),
                     \qquad D\in\mathcal D_{n,a}.
\]
There are only countably many generators.  The evaluation map
\begin{equation}
 q:C\longrightarrow
 Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-common-quotient}
\end{equation}
is a continuous surjection onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
space.

Every \(u_n|_{C\times V}\) is constant on the fibres of
\(q\times\operatorname{id}_V\).  Indeed, suppose \(q(z)=q(z')\) and
\(x\in V\).  Choose a member of
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-local-factor-cover} containing \((z,x)\).
The Boolean coordinates first show that \(z'\in C_{n,a}\), and then that
\(q_{n,a}(z)=q_{n,a}(z')\), since the chosen clopen base separates points.
The local factorization gives \(u_n(z,x)=u_n(z',x)\).  The limit therefore
factors as
\begin{equation}
                           u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x)
                           \qquad(C\times V).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-limit-factor}
\end{equation}

The function \(u\) is upper semicontinuous: each \(u_n\) is locally upper
semicontinuous and
\[
                         \{u<t\}=\bigcup_n\{u_n<t\}.
\]
Upper semicontinuity descends to \(\bar u\) without any unsupported
product-quotient assertion.  If \(\bar u(y,x)<t\), cover the compact fibre
\(q^{-1}(y)\times\{x\}\) by finitely many product neighbourhoods
\(N_j\times D_j\) contained in \(\{u<t\}\).  Set
\(N=\bigcup_jN_j\) and \(D=\bigcap_jD_j\).  Since \(q\) is closed,
\[
                         Y\setminus q(C\setminus N)
\]
is an open neighbourhood of \(y\), and its product with \(D\) lies in
\(\{\bar u<t\}\).

For fixed \(z\), the restrictions \(x\mapsto u_n(z,x)\) are locally
extended-real convex.  The first elementary point makes them convex on
\(V\).  Passing to the limit in every finite convexity inequality shows
that \(x\mapsto u(z,x)\), and hence
\(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\), is extended-real convex.  Thus
\(\mathscr C_X\) is decreasing-sequentially closed.  Since it contains
the generators, minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                         \operatorname{Psh}_X\subseteq\mathscr C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-minimality}
\end{equation}

It remains to prove that every comparison germ is already in the first
stage.  Let \(u\in\mathscr C_X\) have a factorization
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-factorization} on \(C\times V_0\).  Choose a
compact convex polytope \(K\subset V_0\) and a relatively open polyhedral
neighbourhood \(V\) of \(x_0\) such that
\begin{equation}
                         \overline V^{\,P}\subset K\subset V_0.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-nested-core}
\end{equation}
Here the closure is taken in \(P\).  Such a choice is obtained by
intersecting \(P\) with two nested bounded open polyhedral boxes in
\(A\).  We construct every approximant on the one fixed set \(C\times V\).

Give \(Y\times K\) a compatible product metric \(d\).  The upper
semicontinuous function \(\bar u\) is bounded above there; fix an upper
bound \(M\).  For \(k\geq1\), put
\begin{align}
 h_k(s)&=\max\{\bar u(s),-k\},\\
 \Phi_k(s)&=\sup_{t\in Y\times K}
                 \bigl(h_k(t)-k\,d(s,t)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-regularization}
\end{align}
Each \(\Phi_k\) is finite, continuous, and \(k\)-Lipschitz.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                \Phi_{k+1}\leq\Phi_k,\qquad
                \Phi_k\geq\bar u,\qquad
                \Phi_k\downarrow\bar u .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-convergence}
\end{equation}
Only the last assertion requires a check.  Fix \(s\) and a real number
\(a>\bar u(s)\), with \(a\) arbitrary when \(\bar u(s)=-\infty\).
Choose \(b\) with \(\bar u(s)<b<a\).  Upper semicontinuity gives a metric
ball about \(s\) on which \(\bar u<b\).  For large \(k\), also \(-k<b\).
On this ball the expression under the supremum is at most \(b\); outside a
smaller fixed ball it is at most
\(\max\{M,-1\}\) minus \(k\) times a fixed positive number.  It is therefore
less than \(a\) for large \(k\).  This proves the last assertion.

For \(y\in Y\), convexify only in the polyhedral variable:
\begin{equation}
 c_k(y,x)
 =\operatorname{co}_K\bigl(\Phi_k(y,\cdot)\bigr)(x).
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-fibre-convexification}
\end{equation}
Because \(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\) is extended-real convex and
\(\bar u\leq\Phi_k\), every barycentric representation of \(x\) gives
\[
       \bar u(y,x)
       \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\bar u(y,x_i)
       \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\Phi_k(y,x_i).
\]
Taking the infimum yields
\begin{equation}
                     \bar u\leq c_k\leq\Phi_k,
        \qquad       c_{k+1}\leq c_k,
        \qquad       c_k\downarrow\bar u .
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-convexified-convergence}
\end{equation}
The function \(c_k\) is jointly continuous on \(Y\times K\).  Continuity
in \(x\) is the second elementary point.  For \(y,y'\in Y\),
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-envelope-nonexpanding} and the Lipschitz bound
for \(\Phi_k\) give
\[
 \sup_{x\in K}|c_k(y,x)-c_k(y',x)|
 \leq
 \sup_{x\in K}|\Phi_k(y,x)-\Phi_k(y',x)|
 \leq k\,d_Y(y,y'),
\]
after choosing the product metric in sum form.  Separate continuity with
this uniform estimate gives joint continuity.

Choose nested finite clopen partitions \(\mathcal P_k\) of \(Y\) whose
meshes tend to zero.  Such partitions are obtained by taking finite clopen
covers of successively smaller mesh and refining all preceding covers.
For \(Q\in\mathcal P_k\), set
\begin{equation}
             a_{k,Q}(x)=\max_{y\in Q}c_k(y,x),
             \qquad
             a_k(y,x)=a_{k,Q_k(y)}(x),
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-envelope}
\end{equation}
where \(Q_k(y)\) is the member containing \(y\).  Each \(a_{k,Q}\) is a
finite continuous convex function on \(K\).  Refinement and
\(c_{k+1}\leq c_k\) give
\begin{equation}
                              a_{k+1}\leq a_k.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-monotonicity}
\end{equation}
Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
                              a_k\downarrow\bar u
                              \quad\text{on }Y\times K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence}
\end{equation}
The lower bound follows from \(a_k\geq c_k\geq\bar u\).  For the upper
bound, fix \((y,x)\), choose \(a>\bar u(y,x)\), and then choose
\(b\) strictly between these two numbers.  Choose a metric ball on which
\(\bar u<b\).  For large \(k\), the set \(Q_k(y)\times\{x\}\) lies close
enough to \((y,x)\), and \(-k<b\).  In
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-usc-regularization}, points in the chosen ball
contribute at most \(b\), whereas points outside it pay a fixed positive
distance times \(k\).  Consequently
\[
       \sup_{y'\in Q_k(y)}\Phi_k(y',x)<a
\]
for large \(k\).  Since \(a_{k,Q_k(y)}\leq
\sup_{y'\in Q_k(y)}\Phi_k(y',x)\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence}, also at a
\(-\infty\)-valued point.

Put \(\varepsilon_k=4^{-k}\).  The smooth-majorant construction, applied
to the finite family indexed by \(\mathcal P_k\), gives smooth convex
functions \(g_{k,Q}\) on \(A\) such that
\begin{equation}
                        a_{k,Q}\leq g_{k,Q}
                        \leq a_{k,Q}+\varepsilon_k
                        \qquad\text{on }K.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing}
\end{equation}
Define \(w_k\) on \(C\times V\) by
\begin{equation}
                 w_k(z,x)=g_{k,Q}(x)
                 \quad\text{if }q(z)\in Q\in\mathcal P_k.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-smooth-piecewise}
\end{equation}
The inverse images \(q^{-1}(Q)\) form a finite clopen partition of \(C\)
by subsets which are clopen in \(Z\).  Hence \(w_k\) is smooth for the
stated product structure.  Its Hessian in the \(A\)-directions is positive
semidefinite, so \(w_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times V)\).
Equations \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-monotonicity} and
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing} imply
\begin{equation}
                             w_{k+1}\leq w_k+\varepsilon_{k+1}.
 \label{eq:p071-polyhedral-almost-monotone}
\end{equation}

Set
\[
                 \tau_k=\sum_{j\geq k+1}\varepsilon_j,
                 \qquad G_k=w_k+\tau_k .
\]
Since \(\tau_k=\varepsilon_{k+1}+\tau_{k+1}\),
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-almost-monotone} gives
\(G_{k+1}\leq G_k\).  Finally,
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-clopen-convergence},
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-family-smoothing}, and
\(\tau_k\to0\) show that
\[
                         G_k\downarrow u
                         \qquad\text{on }C\times V.
\]
This is \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-fixed-domain}.  We have proved
\[
                         \mathscr C_X
                         \subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-minimality} and the tautological
inclusion
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_X\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-polyhedral-collapse}.

The proof is local and uses only the generator sheaf.  It therefore
transports through any generator-preserving chart and proves the asserted
chartwise extension.  For a rational convex polyhedron with its induced
Chambert--Loir--Ducros affine tropical structure, smooth functions are
locally restrictions of ambient smooth functions; positivity of
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''f\) is positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian on
the affine span.  A locally constant affine structure on \(Z\) becomes
constant after a clopen shrinking, and the product construction gives
exactly the generator sheaf used above.  This verifies the claimed
compatibility while leaving untouched the excluded nonconvex and branched
settings.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p071-exact-star-polyhedral-envelope}
Let \(A\) be finite and \(K\) countable.  Let \(D\) be the compact exact-star
core having exceptional branches \([-R_a,0]\), \(a\in A\), full branches
\([-\infty,0]\), \(b\in K\), and common node \(\eta\).  Let \(Q\) be a
nonempty compact convex polytope.

Write \(\mathcal A(D\times Q)\) for the continuous real-valued functions
whose restrictions to every branch prism are jointly convex and which
satisfy the exact reciprocal-weight product junction inequalities: for every
finite \(F\subset K\), admissible \(r_b>0\), \(0<\rho_a\leq R_a\), and
points \(y_0,y_b,y_a\in Q\) with
\[
 \Lambda y_0=
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{y_b}{r_b}
   +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{y_a}{\rho_a},
 \qquad
 \Lambda=\sum_{b\in F}\frac1{r_b}
            +\sum_{a\in A}\frac1{\rho_a}>0,
\]
one has
\[
 \Lambda v(\eta,y_0)\leq
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{v_b(-r_b,y_b)}{r_b}
   +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{v_a(-\rho_a,y_a)}{\rho_a}.
\]
For \(\phi\in C(D\times Q)\), define
\begin{equation}
 C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi(x)=
 \sup\{v(x):v\in\mathcal A(D\times Q),\ v\leq\phi\}.
 \label{eq:p071-exact-envelope-definition}
\end{equation}
Then \(C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi\) belongs to
\(\mathcal A(D\times Q)\), is the largest member of that class below
\(\phi\), and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \lVert C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi-C^{\mathrm{ex}}\psi\rVert_{D\times Q}
 \leq \lVert\phi-\psi\rVert_{D\times Q}
 \qquad(\phi,\psi\in C(D\times Q)).
 \label{eq:p071-exact-envelope-nonexpanding}
\end{equation}
In particular the envelope is continuous simultaneously at the star node,
the full endpoints, and every face of \(Q\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The defining family is nonempty because it contains every constant below
\(\min\phi\).  Hence \(C:=C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi\) is finite,
\(\min\phi\leq C\leq\phi\), and is lower semicontinuous as a supremum of
continuous functions.  A pointwise supremum preserves joint convexity on
every branch prism.  It also preserves the junction inequalities: apply the
inequality to one competitor before taking its supremum at the centre, and
then bound the supremum of the weighted sum by the weighted sum of the
pointwise suprema.  Since the set of full branches is countable, the common
countable-activity condition is automatic on this reduced core.

We prove the full-endpoint trace together with the uniform estimate needed
for continuity.  Fix \(b\in K\) and \(\delta>0\).  Continuity of \(\phi_b\)
on the compact product \([-\infty,0]\times Q\) gives a \(T<0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \lvert\phi_b(t,y)-\phi_b(-\infty,y)\rvert<\delta/3
 \quad(t\leq T,\ y\in Q).
 \label{eq:p071-exact-envelope-obstacle-terminal-control}
\end{equation}
Every competitor \(v\) is nondecreasing along a full branch: a finite convex
function of \(t\in(-\infty,0]\) having a finite limit at \(-\infty\) has
nonnegative secant slopes.  Put
\[
                         e_v(y)=v_b(T,y)-\delta
\]
and define \(w\) by \(w=v-\delta\) off branch \(b\), while on that branch
set
\begin{equation}
                  w_b(t,y)=
          \max\{v_b(t,y)-\delta,e_v(y)\}.
 \label{eq:p071-exact-envelope-terminal-repair}
\end{equation}
The function \(e_v\) is continuous and convex.  Moreover
\(e_v\leq v(\eta,\cdot)-\delta\), so the common node value of \(w\) is
still \(v(\eta,\cdot)-\delta\).  Thus \(w\) is continuous and jointly
convex on every branch.  A common downward translation preserves every
junction inequality, and the subsequent increase on one full branch only
increases its right-hand side.  Hence \(w\) satisfies all junction
inequalities.

For \(t\geq T\), monotonicity gives
\(w_b(t,y)=v_b(t,y)-\delta\leq\phi_b(t,y)\).  For \(t\leq T\),
\eqref{eq:p071-exact-envelope-obstacle-terminal-control} gives
\[
 e_v(y)\leq\phi_b(T,y)-\delta
 <\phi_b(-\infty,y)-2\delta/3
 <\phi_b(t,y),
\]
while the other entry in
\eqref{eq:p071-exact-envelope-terminal-repair} is also below \(\phi_b\).
Consequently \(w\leq\phi\) on the whole compact product, and \(w\) is an
admissible competitor.  Its endpoint value is \(e_v\), so
\[
 C(-\infty,y)\geq v_b(T,y)-\delta.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(v\), and using monotonicity once more, yields
\begin{equation}
 0\leq C_b(t,y)-C_b(-\infty,y)\leq\delta
 \quad(t\leq T,\ y\in Q).
 \label{eq:p071-exact-envelope-uniform-terminal-trace}
\end{equation}
Thus \(C\) has the exact endpoint trace, uniformly in the polyhedral
variable.

On every finite branch prism, \(C\) is finite, convex, and lower
semicontinuous.  A finite convex function on a compact polytope is upper
semicontinuous: triangulate locally with the chosen point as a vertex and
let its barycentric coefficient tend to one.  Hence \(C\) is continuous on
every finite branch prism.  The endpoint slice is likewise finite, convex,
and lower semicontinuous on \(Q\), hence continuous; the uniform estimate
\eqref{eq:p071-exact-envelope-uniform-terminal-trace} then gives joint
continuity at each full endpoint.

It remains only to check the common node.  On a full branch, the same
monotonicity gives
\[
                         C_b(t,y)\leq C(\eta,y).
\]
The node slice is continuous by the preceding compact-polytope argument.
Along any sequence converging to the node, each subsequence either has a
further subsequence in one fixed branch, where branch-prism continuity
applies, or has a further subsequence whose full-branch labels escape every
finite set, where the last display gives the required upper bound.  Lower
semicontinuity of \(C\) gives the opposite bound.  Therefore \(C\) is
continuous at the node as well.

We have shown that \(C\in\mathcal A(D\times Q)\).  Since \(C\leq\phi\), it
is itself a member of the family in
\eqref{eq:p071-exact-envelope-definition}, and hence is its largest member.
Finally, if
\(\lVert\phi-\psi\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), then
\(C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi-\varepsilon\) is a comparison function below
\(\psi\).  Maximality gives
\(C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi-\varepsilon\leq C^{\mathrm{ex}}\psi\); interchanging
\(\phi\) and \(\psi\) proves
\eqref{eq:p071-exact-envelope-nonexpanding}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p071-terminal-polyhedral-insertion}
Let \(Q\) be a nonempty compact convex polytope, let \(R\in\mathbf R\), and
put
\[
                       L=[-\infty,R]\times Q.
\]
Suppose that \(u:L\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is upper semicontinuous,
jointly extended-real convex on the finite stratum, nondecreasing in the
first variable, and has the exact pointwise trace at \(-\infty\).  If
\(\phi\in C(L)\) and \(u\leq\phi\), then there is a continuous real-valued
function \(E_\phi\) on \(L\), jointly convex on the finite stratum,
nondecreasing in the first variable, and having the exact endpoint trace,
such that
\begin{equation}
                             u\leq E_\phi\leq\phi.
 \label{eq:p071-terminal-insertion-sandwich}
\end{equation}
Moreover, \(E_\phi\) is the largest function with these properties below
\(\phi\), and the operator \(\phi\mapsto E_\phi\) is nondecreasing and
nonexpanding in the uniform norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For a finite point \((t,y)\), let
\begin{equation}
 E_\phi(t,y)=
 \inf\left\{
   \sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i\phi(t_i,y_i):
   \begin{array}{l}
    q<\infty,\quad \alpha_i\geq0,\quad \sum_i\alpha_i=1,\\
    t_i\in\mathbf R,\quad t_i\leq R,\quad y_i\in Q,\\
    \sum_i\alpha_i t_i\geq t,\quad
    \sum_i\alpha_i y_i=y
   \end{array}\right\}.
 \label{eq:p071-terminal-monotone-convex-envelope}
\end{equation}
At the endpoint, put
\begin{align}
 m(y)&=\min_{s\in[-\infty,R]}\phi(s,y),\\
 E_\phi(-\infty,y)
   &=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i m(y_i):
       q<\infty,\ \alpha_i\geq0,\ \sum_i\alpha_i=1,\
       \sum_i\alpha_i y_i=y\right\}.
 \label{eq:p071-terminal-endpoint-envelope}
\end{align}
The second expression is the ordinary convex envelope of \(m\) on \(Q\).
The function \(m\) is continuous, since uniform continuity of \(\phi\) on
\(L\) controls its minimum uniformly in the parameter \(y\).

The singleton measure shows that \(E_\phi\leq\phi\) at every point.  Mixtures
of admissible families in
\eqref{eq:p071-terminal-monotone-convex-envelope} show that \(E_\phi\) is
jointly convex on the finite stratum.  Enlarging the lower bound imposed on
the mean of the \(t_i\) shrinks the admissible family, so \(E_\phi\) is
nondecreasing in \(t\).

We next prove continuity away from the endpoint.  For \(N>-R\), restrict
\eqref{eq:p071-terminal-monotone-convex-envelope} to
\(t_i\in[-N,R]\), and denote the resulting envelope by \(E_{\phi,N}\).
For this truncated problem the same infimum is obtained if arbitrary Borel
probability measures on \([-N,R]\times Q\) are allowed.  Indeed,
Carath\'eodory's theorem, applied to the vector consisting of the
\(t\)-coordinate, the affine coordinates on \(Q\), and the value of \(\phi\),
replaces any such measure by a finitely supported measure with the same two
moments and the same cost.  The full probability-measure space is compact in
the weak topology, and the moment conditions are closed.  Hence a convergent
sequence of roots and minimizing measures proves lower semicontinuity.  The
function is finite and convex on the compact polytope \([-N,R]\times Q\), so
a triangulation having any prescribed boundary point as a vertex gives upper
semicontinuity there.  Thus \(E_{\phi,N}\) is continuous.

Set
\[
 \omega_N=\sup\{
   |\phi(s,y)-\phi(s',y)|:
   s,s'\in[-\infty,-N],\ y\in Q\}.
\]
Continuity on the compactification gives \(\omega_N\to0\).  Since the
restricted admissible family is smaller,
\[
                         E_\phi\leq E_{\phi,N}
                         \quad\text{on }[-N,R]\times Q.
\]
Conversely, in any admissible finite family for \(E_\phi(t,y)\), replace
each \(t_i<-N\) by \(-N\).  This only increases its \(t\)-mean, preserves
its \(Q\)-barycentre, and changes its cost by at most \(\omega_N\).
Taking infima gives
\begin{equation}
 0\leq E_{\phi,N}-E_\phi\leq\omega_N
 \quad\text{on }[-N,R]\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-terminal-finite-truncation}
\end{equation}
On every fixed finite subprism, the right side tends to zero.  Hence
\(E_\phi\) is continuous at every finite point.

The endpoint formula is also continuous in \(y\): the convex envelope of a
continuous function on a compact polytope is finite and continuous.  Every
family admissible in
\eqref{eq:p071-terminal-monotone-convex-envelope} gives
\[
 E_\phi(-\infty,y)
 \leq\sum_i\alpha_i m(y_i)
 \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\phi(t_i,y_i),
\]
and therefore \(E_\phi(-\infty,y)\leq E_\phi(t,y)\).
For the reverse estimate, choose a minimizing finite representation of
\(E_\phi(-\infty,y)\).  It exists by the same compactness and Carath\'eodory
argument, now on \(Q\).  For each \(y_i\), choose a point \(s_i\) where
\(m(y_i)=\phi(s_i,y_i)\).  Replace every
\(s_i<-N\), including \(s_i=-\infty\), by \(-N\).  The resulting family
has \(t\)-mean at least \(-N\), and its cost increases by at most
\(\omega_N\).  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 0\leq E_\phi(t,y)-E_\phi(-\infty,y)\leq\omega_N
 \quad(t\leq-N,\ y\in Q).
 \label{eq:p071-terminal-uniform-endpoint}
\end{equation}
This proves both the exact trace and joint continuity at the endpoint.

It remains to prove the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:p071-terminal-insertion-sandwich}.  For a finite root and a family
in
\eqref{eq:p071-terminal-monotone-convex-envelope}, monotonicity followed by
convexity gives
\[
 u(t,y)\leq
 u\left(\sum_i\alpha_i t_i,\sum_i\alpha_i y_i\right)
 \leq\sum_i\alpha_i u(t_i,y_i)
 \leq\sum_i\alpha_i\phi(t_i,y_i).
\]
By the exact trace, the endpoint slice is the pointwise decreasing limit, as
\(t\to-\infty\), of the convex slices \(u(t,\cdot)\); it is therefore
extended-real convex.  At the endpoint, monotonicity and this convexity give
\[
 u(-\infty,y)\leq
 \sum_i\alpha_i u(-\infty,y_i)
 \leq\sum_i\alpha_i m(y_i).
\]
Taking the two infima proves \(u\leq E_\phi\).

The same two Jensen calculations apply to every jointly convex,
nondecreasing function with exact trace below \(\phi\).  Such a function is
therefore bounded above by \(E_\phi\).  Since the preceding paragraphs show
that \(E_\phi\) itself has all the required properties, it is the largest
one.  Monotonicity in the obstacle is immediate from the two infimum
formulas.  If \(\lVert\phi-\psi\rVert_\infty\leq\delta\), every admissible
cost for one obstacle differs from the corresponding cost for the other by
at most \(\delta\).  Hence
\(\lVert E_\phi-E_\psi\rVert_\infty\leq\delta\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p071-finite-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion}
Let \(A\) and \(F\) be disjoint finite sets with \(A\cup F\ne\varnothing\).
Form a compact exact star \(D\) with centre \(\eta\), exceptional branches
\[
                  [0,R_a]\quad(a\in A),
\]
and full branches
\[
                  [0,+\infty]\quad(b\in F),
\]
all parameterized outwards from \(\eta\).  Let \(Q\) be a nonempty compact
convex polytope.

Suppose that \(u:D\times Q\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) is upper
semicontinuous, is jointly extended-real convex on every finite branch
prism, is nonincreasing in the radial variable on every full branch, and
has the exact trace at each full endpoint.  Write
\(c(y)=u(\eta,y)\), and assume the following exact product junction
inequalities.  For every \(S\subseteq F\), every choice of positive radii
\(s_i\) on the branches \(i\in A\cup S\), and points \(y_i\in Q\), put
\[
 \Lambda=\sum_{i\in A\cup S}\frac1{s_i},
 \qquad
 y_0=\Lambda^{-1}\sum_{i\in A\cup S}\frac{y_i}{s_i}.
\]
Whenever \(\Lambda>0\) and \(c(y_0)\) is finite, require
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda c(y_0)\leq
       \sum_{i\in A\cup S}\frac{u_i(s_i,y_i)}{s_i}.
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-star-junction}
\end{equation}

If \(\phi\in C(D\times Q)\) and \(u\leq\phi\), then there is a largest
exact product-comparison function \(E_\phi\) below \(\phi\).  It is
real-valued and continuous on \(D\times Q\), including every full endpoint,
and
\begin{equation}
                              u\leq E_\phi\leq\phi.
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-star-insertion}
\end{equation}
Moreover, the operator \(\phi\mapsto E_\phi\) is nondecreasing and
nonexpanding in the uniform norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We first give the Jensen families defining the envelope.  A finite atomic
probability measure \(\mu\) will be supported at node points
\((\eta,y)\) and at finite branch points \((i,s,y)\).  Put
\[
 q_i(\mu)=\int_{\{i\}\times(0,\infty)\times Q}s\,\mathrm d\mu,
 \qquad
 \bar y(\mu)=\int y\,\mathrm d\mu.
\]
For a node root \((\eta,y)\), call \(\mu\) admissible if
\(\bar y(\mu)=y\) and there is a number \(\lambda\geq0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 q_a(\mu)=\lambda\quad(a\in A),
 \qquad
 q_b(\mu)\leq\lambda\quad(b\in F).
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-node-moments}
\end{equation}
For a finite point \((a_0,s,y)\) on an exceptional branch, replace the
first group of equalities by
\begin{equation}
 q_{a_0}(\mu)=s+\lambda,\qquad
 q_a(\mu)=\lambda\quad(a\in A\setminus\{a_0\}),
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-exception-moments}
\end{equation}
and retain the full-branch inequalities in
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-node-moments}.  For a finite point
\((b_0,s,y)\) on a full branch, require
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 q_a(\mu)&=\lambda \quad(a\in A),\\
 q_b(\mu)&\leq\lambda \quad(b\in F\setminus\{b_0\}),\\
 q_{b_0}(\mu)&\leq s+\lambda .
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-full-moments}
\end{equation}
At the endpoint \((b_0,+\infty,y)\), impose the first two lines of
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-full-moments} and no upper bound on
\(q_{b_0}(\mu)\).  Denote the resulting family by
\(\mathcal J_x\), where \(x\) is the root, and define
\begin{equation}
             E_\phi(x)=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal J_x}\int\phi\,\mathrm d\mu.
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-moment-envelope}
\end{equation}
Every finite-root family contains the singleton at its root.  At a full
endpoint, singletons at finite points of that branch are admissible and
approach the endpoint.  Thus the families are nonempty and the envelope is
finite.

We next prove continuity.  For \(N\geq1\), restrict the support of every
measure on a full branch to radii at most \(N\), allow arbitrary Borel
probability measures on the resulting compact finite star, and call the
corresponding value \(E_{\phi,N}\).  This does not change the value if one
restricts again to finite atomic measures.  Indeed, Carath\'eodory's theorem
applied to all radial moments, the affine coordinates on \(Q\), and the
cost replaces any probability measure by a finite one with the same data.

The admissible-measure correspondence for \(E_{\phi,N}\) is compact-valued
and closed.  When \(A\ne\varnothing\), the common number \(\lambda\) is one
of the bounded exceptional radial moments.  When \(A=\varnothing\), the
existential inequalities impose no additional closedness issue.  Therefore
convergent roots and minimizing measures give lower semicontinuity.
Mixtures of admissible measures show joint convexity on every branch prism.
On a full branch, increasing the root radius relaxes only the last
inequality in \eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-full-moments}; hence
\(E_{\phi,N}\) is nonincreasing there.  It is constant for root radii
\(s\geq N\), including at \(+\infty\).  A finite convex function on a
compact polytope is upper semicontinuous at its boundary by a triangulation
with the target point as a vertex.  Consequently \(E_{\phi,N}\) is
continuous on each branch prism.  The moment conditions at radius zero are
exactly \eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-node-moments}; since there are only
finitely many branches, the branchwise continuities glue at the node.

Set
\[
 \omega_N=\max_{b\in F}\sup\{
   |\phi_b(s,y)-\phi_b(s',y)|:
   s,s'\in[N,+\infty],\ y\in Q\},
\]
with \(\omega_N=0\) when \(F=\varnothing\).  Continuity on the finitely many
compactified full prisms gives \(\omega_N\to0\).  The restricted measure
family is smaller, so \(E_\phi\leq E_{\phi,N}\).  Conversely, in a finite
family admissible for \(E_\phi(x)\), replace every full-branch radius
\(s>N\) by \(N\), without changing its mass or its \(Q\)-coordinate.
Every full radial moment decreases.  All full moment conditions in
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-node-moments} and
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-full-moments} are upper bounds, so the new
family is still admissible.  Its cost changes by at most \(\omega_N\).
Taking infima gives the uniform estimate
\begin{equation}
             0\leq E_{\phi,N}-E_\phi\leq\omega_N
             \quad\text{on }D\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-uniform-truncation}
\end{equation}
Thus \(E_\phi\) is a uniform limit of continuous functions and is
continuous on the whole compact product.  The singleton inequalities at
finite points and passage to a full endpoint now give \(E_\phi\leq\phi\).

We verify that \(E_\phi\) satisfies the comparison conditions.  Convexity
on branch prisms follows by mixing root measures and their corresponding
\(\lambda\)'s.  The same mixing and
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-full-moments} show that the envelope is
nonincreasing on a full branch.  Its exact endpoint trace follows from
continuity.

For the junction condition, normalize the weights in
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-star-junction} by putting
\[
                       \alpha_i=\frac1{\Lambda s_i}.
\]
Choose nearly minimizing measures \(\mu_i\) for the branch roots and let
\(\lambda_i\) be their moment parameters.  Their mixture
\(\mu=\sum_i\alpha_i\mu_i\) has the prescribed \(Q\)-barycentre.  Put
\[
                  L=\sum_i\alpha_i\lambda_i,
                  \qquad q_0=\alpha_i s_i=\Lambda^{-1}.
\]
For every exceptional branch its radial moment in \(\mu\) equals
\(L+q_0\).  For an included full branch the moment is at most \(L+q_0\),
and for an omitted full branch it is at most \(L\).  Hence \(\mu\) is
admissible for the node root, with parameter \(L+q_0\).  Formula
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-moment-envelope}, followed by the
near-minimizing limit, gives
\[
                   E_\phi(\eta,y_0)
                      \leq\sum_i\alpha_iE_{\phi,i}(s_i,y_i),
\]
which is precisely the required junction inequality.

It remains to prove that the moment families encode every consequence of
the primitive comparison inequalities.  We prove the following Jensen
claim:
\begin{equation}
             v(x)\leq\int v\,\mathrm d\mu
 \quad\text{for every exact comparison function \(v\leq\phi\) and
 every \(\mu\in\mathcal J_x\).}
 \label{eq:p071-finite-exact-jensen-claim}
\end{equation}
It is enough to treat finite real-valued $v$.  Indeed, if $v\leq\phi$,
choose constants $K_j<\min\phi$ with $K_j\downarrow-\infty$, and put
$v_j=\max\{v,K_j\}$.  Each $v_j$ is finite, remains below $\phi$,
and satisfies all comparison conditions: the scalar maximum map is convex
and nondecreasing, so it preserves every normalized Jensen inequality.
The finite-valued claim gives
\[
                         v_j(x)\leq\int v_j\,\mathrm d\mu.
\]
The measure $\mu$ has finite support.  Hence the left side decreases to
$v(x)$, while the right side decreases to the extended-real finite sum
$\int v\,\mathrm d\mu$, with zero-weight atoms omitted.  Passing to the
limit proves the claim for $v$.

First let the root be a node.  Ignore atoms of \(\mu\) at radius zero.
For each branch, partition an interval of length \(q_i(\mu)\) into pieces
of lengths equal to the atom weights times their radii, and label every
piece by the corresponding atom.  Use \([0,\lambda]\) for each exceptional
branch and place the labelled interval of a full branch inside
\([0,\lambda]\), which is possible by
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-node-moments}.  At almost every
\(\tau\in[0,\lambda]\), select the labelled atom on every exceptional
branch and on each full branch whose labelled set contains \(\tau\).
Writing the selected atom as \((i,s_i(\tau),y_i(\tau))\), apply
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-star-junction} with reciprocal weights
\(1/s_i(\tau)\).  After integration in \(\tau\), every positive-radius
atom of weight \(\beta\) contributes exactly
\[
             \int_{\text{its interval}}\frac{\mathrm d\tau}{s}
                   =\beta
\]
times its value and its \(Q\)-coordinate.  Convexity of the centre slice
combines the integrated centre values, and a second application of that
convexity combines the original radius-zero atoms.  Since
\(\bar y(\mu)=y\), the result is
\[
                         c(y)\leq\int v\,\mathrm d\mu.
\]
This also covers \(A=\varnothing\); values of \(\tau\) at which no branch
is selected contribute zero.

Now let the root lie on a branch \(i_0\) at radius \(s\).  If \(i_0\in A\),
put \(r=s\).  If \(i_0\in F\), put
\[
                         r=\max\{0,q_{i_0}(\mu)-\lambda\}\leq s.
\]
Choose a submeasure \(\nu\) of the \(i_0\)-branch part of \(\mu\) whose
radial moment is \(r\), splitting one atom if necessary.  The residual
measure \(\mu-\nu\), after normalization when it has positive mass,
satisfies the node moment conditions.  If
\(\beta=\nu(D\times Q)\) and both \(\beta\) and \(1-\beta\) are positive,
branchwise Jensen and the node case give
\[
 v_{i_0}\left(r,\bar y(\mu)\right)
   \leq \int v\,\mathrm d\mu;
\]
more explicitly, this is branch convexity between the barycentre of
\(\nu/\beta\), whose weighted radial coordinate is \(r\), and the node
barycentre of the normalized residual measure.  If \(\beta=0\), then
\(r=0\) and the node case gives the same inequality; if \(\beta=1\), it is
ordinary branchwise Jensen.  On an exceptional branch
\(r=s\).  On a full branch \(r\leq s\), so radial nonincrease gives
\[
 v_{i_0}(s,\bar y(\mu))
       \leq v_{i_0}(r,\bar y(\mu))
       \leq\int v\,\mathrm d\mu.
\]
At a full endpoint, apply the finite-root inequality for every sufficiently
large \(s\) and use the exact trace.  This proves
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-jensen-claim}.

Apply the Jensen claim to \(u\) and then take the infimum in
\eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-moment-envelope}; this proves the first
inequality in \eqref{eq:p071-finite-exact-star-insertion}.  The same claim
shows that every exact comparison function below \(\phi\) is bounded above
by \(E_\phi\), so the envelope is largest.  Monotonicity in the obstacle is
immediate from the formula.  If
\(\|\phi-\psi\|_\infty\leq\delta\), integration over probability measures
gives
\(\|E_\phi-E_\psi\|_\infty\leq\delta\), proving nonexpansion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p071-arbitrary-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion}
Let \(D\) be a compact standard core in an exact CLD star, with finite
exceptional set \(A\) and an arbitrary set \(B\setminus A\) of full
branches, and let \(Q\) be a nonempty compact convex polytope.  For
\(\phi\in C(D\times Q)\), let
\[
 C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi
   =\sup\left\{v:v\leq\phi,\
       \substack{v\text{ is a continuous exact product-comparison}\\
                 \text{function on }D\times Q}\right\}.
\]
If \(u\leq\phi\) is any upper-semicontinuous exact product-comparison
function, then
\begin{equation}
                         u\leq C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi.
 \label{eq:p071-arbitrary-star-envelope-dominates}
\end{equation}
If \(B\setminus A\) is countable, the continuous-cone envelope of
\Cref{lem:p071-exact-star-polyhedral-envelope} is consequently the largest
comparison minorant of \(\phi\), even when discontinuous comparison
minorants are allowed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(x\in D\times Q\) and \(\delta>0\).  Continuity of \(\phi\) at the
node, uniformly over the compact set \(Q\), gives a finite set
\(F\subset B\setminus A\) such that
\begin{equation}
 |\phi_b(s,y)-\phi(\eta,y)|<\delta
 \quad
 \bigl(b\in B\setminus(A\cup F),\
       s\in[0,+\infty],\ y\in Q\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-arbitrary-star-cofinite-obstacle}
\end{equation}
Indeed, otherwise a net of points on branches escaping every finite set,
together with a convergent subnet of their \(Q\)-coordinates, would
converge to a node point while violating continuity.  Enlarge \(F\) to
contain the full branch of \(x\), if \(x\) lies on one.

Restrict \(u\) and \(\phi\) to the finite exact substar consisting of all
exceptional branches and the branches in \(F\).
\Cref{lem:p071-finite-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion} gives a continuous
exact comparison function \(h\) there such that
\[
                              u\leq h\leq\phi.
\]
Extend \(h\) to the full core by setting every branch outside \(F\) equal
to its centre slice \(h_0(y)=h(\eta,y)\), and then subtract \(\delta\)
globally.  Call the result \(v\).  It is continuous at the node because
only finitely many branches are active, and it has the exact trace at every
full endpoint.  On an inactive branch,
\[
 v_b(s,y)=h_0(y)-\delta
       \leq\phi(\eta,y)-\delta
       <\phi_b(s,y)
\]
by \eqref{eq:p071-arbitrary-star-cofinite-obstacle}; on the finite substar
the inequality \(v\leq\phi\) is immediate.

We check the global junction inequality.  In a prescribed junction tuple,
split the sampled full branches into the active set \(S\subseteq F\) and
the inactive set \(T\).  Let \(\Lambda_0\) be the total reciprocal weight
of all exceptional and active samples, and let \(\Theta\) be that of the
inactive samples.  If \(\Lambda_0>0\), denote by \(y_*\) the barycentre of
the exceptional and active samples.  The finite-substar junction inequality
and convexity of \(h_0\) give
\[
 \begin{split}
  (\Lambda_0+\Theta)h_0(y_0)
  &\leq \Lambda_0h_0(y_*)
       +\sum_{b\in T}\frac{h_0(y_b)}{s_b}\\
  &\leq
       \sum_{i\in A\cup S}\frac{h_i(s_i,y_i)}{s_i}
       +\sum_{b\in T}\frac{h_0(y_b)}{s_b}.
 \end{split}
\]
If \(\Lambda_0=0\), the same conclusion is simply convexity of \(h_0\).
Global translation by \(-\delta\) preserves the inequality because the
reciprocal weights on both sides have the same sum.  Thus \(v\) is a
continuous exact product-comparison minorant of \(\phi\).

The chosen point belongs to the finite substar, so
\[
                         v(x)=h(x)-\delta\geq u(x)-\delta.
\]
It follows that
\(C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi(x)\geq u(x)-\delta\).  Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\)
proves \eqref{eq:p071-arbitrary-star-envelope-dominates}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
We use the exact scalar star theorem
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate} and the compact-core
envelope lemmas
\Cref{lem:p071-exact-star-polyhedral-envelope,%
lem:p071-arbitrary-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion}.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The comparison sheaf and the easy inclusion.}
Upper semicontinuity, branchwise joint convexity, and the endpoint trace are
local.  The junction inequality is local by the same contraction calculation
as in the open-Euclidean product.  Namely, contract every sample by a common
factor \(0<s<1\) towards \((\eta,y_0)\):
\[
 (-r_i,y_i)\longmapsto
       (-sr_i,\,y_0+s(y_i-y_0)).
\]
The barycentre relation is preserved and every reciprocal weight is
multiplied by \(s^{-1}\).  If restriction makes finitely many formerly full
branches exceptional, add samples on them with polyhedral coordinate
\(y_0\).  Their values are at most the centre value.  Branchwise convexity
bounds every contracted original sample by
\[
 (1-s)c(y_0)+s\,u_i(-r_i,y_i).
\]
Substitution in the restricted-chart inequality and cancellation of the
added central terms recover
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-junction} on the original chart.  Thus
\(\mathcal J_X\) is a sheaf.

It is closed under pointwise decreasing sequential limits.  Such a limit is
upper semicontinuous and jointly extended-real convex on every branch.
The exact full-endpoint trace passes by monotonicity: one inequality is
immediate, while one sufficiently advanced row gives the reverse inequality,
also when the endpoint value is \(-\infty\).  At a node, fix a compact
polytope \(Q\) in one comparison chart.  For each row, finitely many charts
cover \(\{\eta\}\times Q\); the union of their finite exceptional and
countable activity sets is countable.  Taking the union over the rows gives
one countable activity set for the limit.

If the limiting centre value in a prescribed junction tuple is finite, then
the centre values of all rows are finite.  The rowwise junction inequality
forces every sampled row value to be finite, since no term may equal
\(+\infty\).  None of these sampled values can tend to \(-\infty\): all
other terms are bounded above by their first-row values, so the right side
would tend to \(-\infty\) while the left side has a finite limit.  Termwise
passage to the limit proves the junction inequality.  Hence
\(\mathcal J_X\) is decreasing-sequentially closed.

Every generator belongs to \(\mathcal J_X\).  Only the junction inequality
needs comment.  Put \(d_i=\partial_tg_i(0,y_0)\).  Joint convexity gives
\[
 g_i(-r_i,y_i)\geq
 c_g(y_0)-r_id_i+
 \nabla c_g(y_0)\mathbin\cdot(y_i-y_0).
\]
After division by \(r_i\), the polyhedral linear terms cancel by
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-barycentre}.  Every omitted full-branch
derivative is nonnegative, and
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-balance} therefore makes the sum
of the selected derivatives nonpositive.  This is exactly
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-junction}.  Minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                           \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal J_X.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-easy-inclusion}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Continuous decreasing envelope rows at a node.}
Fix \(u\in\mathcal J_X\) near \((\eta,y_0)\).  Choose a comparison chart
\(U\times V_0\), with finite exceptional set \(A\) and countable activity
set \(K\).  Shrink the exceptional collars once and let \(D\subset U\) be
the resulting compact closed standard core.  Choose a relatively open
convex set \(V\subset P\) and a compact convex polytope \(Q\subset P\) such
that
\[
            y_0\in V,\qquad
            \overline V^{\,P}\subset Q\subset V_0.
\]
Collapse every full branch outside \(A\cup K\) to the node.  The resulting
compact exact star \(D_K\) is metrizable, and \(u|_{D\times Q}\) factors
through \(D_K\times Q\).

Fix a compatible metric \(d\) on this compact product and set
\begin{equation}
 \phi_n(z)=\sup_w
   \bigl(\max\{u(w),-n\}-n\,d(z,w)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-upper-regularization}
\end{equation}
These functions are finite and continuous,
\(\phi_{n+1}\leq\phi_n\), and \(\phi_n\downarrow u\).  Define
\[
                         H_n=C^{\mathrm{ex}}\phi_n.
\]
The compact-envelope lemma gives a finite continuous exact comparison
function and monotonicity in the obstacle.  The insertion lemma gives
\(u\leq H_n\), while the defining minorant property gives
\(H_n\leq\phi_n\).  Therefore
\begin{equation}
             H_{n+1}\leq H_n,\qquad H_n\downarrow u
             \quad\text{on }D_K\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-envelope-rows}
\end{equation}
Lift \(H_n\) to \(D\times Q\) by making every branch outside \(K\) equal
to its node slice.  The two-stage barycentre calculation in
\Cref{lem:p071-arbitrary-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion} shows that the
lift is still an exact product comparison function.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-envelope-rows} remain valid after the
lift.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite activity and a uniform smooth majorant.}
We first record a uniform approximation statement for one finite continuous
row \(H\) on \(D\times Q\).  Since a full branch is nonincreasing outwards,
\[
                         H_b(t,y)\leq H(\eta,y).
\]
Continuity at the node in the cofinite-branch topology, uniformly over the
compact set \(Q\), implies that for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a finite
set \(F_\varepsilon\subset K\) such that replacing every branch outside
\(A\cup F_\varepsilon\) by the node slice produces a finite-active comparison
function \(\widetilde H\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
                 H\leq\widetilde H\leq H+\varepsilon
                 \quad\text{on }D\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-finite-activity-error}
\end{equation}
The junction condition survives this replacement even when an inactive
sample has a different polyhedral coordinate: first apply the finite-substar
junction inequality at the barycentre of the exceptional and active
samples, then combine that point with the inactive coordinates by convexity
of the node slice.

Choose once a smaller standard neighbourhood \(U'\) whose closure is
contained in the interior of the chosen core.  We claim that there is an
ambient function \(W\) on \(U'\times L_P\), whose restriction to
\(U'\times V\) is a generator, such that
\begin{equation}
               \widetilde H\leq W\leq\widetilde H+5\varepsilon
               \quad\text{on }\overline{U'}\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}
\end{equation}
Choose an origin in \(L_P\).  For \(p\in L_P^*\), put
\begin{align}
 f_0(p)&=\min_{y\in Q}
       \bigl(\widetilde H(\eta,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),\\
 f_b(t,p)&=\min_{y\in Q}
       \bigl(\widetilde H_b(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-scalar-profiles}
\end{align}
For each \(p\), these functions form a finite, continuous, finite-active
member of the scalar exact-star comparison class.  Branch convexity follows
by combining minimizing polyhedral points.  The endpoint trace passes
through the minimum by uniform continuity on the compact terminal prism.
For the scalar junction inequality, choose minimizing points for the finitely
many branch terms and use their reciprocal-weight barycentre as a competitor
in the node minimum.

For fixed \(b\) and \(t\), extend the slice
\(\widetilde H_b(t,\cdot)\) by \(+\infty\) off \(Q\).  The extension is
proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \(L_P\), including at every face
and corner because \(\widetilde H\) is continuous on the closed polytope.
Fenchel--Moreau gives
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde H_b(t,y)=
       \sup_{p\in L_P^*}\bigl(p\mathbin\cdot y+f_b(t,p)\bigr)
 \qquad(y\in Q),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-fenchel}
\end{equation}
with the analogous formula at the node and full endpoints.

At each point of the compact product
\(\overline{U'}\times Q\), choose a covector realizing
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-fenchel} within \(\varepsilon\).
For fixed \(p\), the profile \(f(\,\cdot\,,p)\) is continuous on the star,
so one covector works on a neighbourhood.  A finite subcover gives
\(p_1,\ldots,p_q\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde H-\varepsilon\leq
 A_0:=\max_j\bigl(p_j\mathbin\cdot y+f(x,p_j)\bigr)
 \leq\widetilde H.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-finite-dual-sampling}
\end{equation}

For each selected covector, the finite harmonic smoothing in the scalar
exact-star theorem gives a smooth psh profile \(s_j\) on the same \(U'\)
with
\[
             \lVert s_j-f(\,\cdot\,,p_j)\rVert_{\overline{U'}}
                    <\varepsilon.
\]
Lift these profiles to
\[
               s_j(x)+p_j\mathbin\cdot y+2\varepsilon.
\]
Their maximum lies between \(\widetilde H\) and
\(\widetilde H+3\varepsilon\).  Apply a smooth convex coordinatewise
nondecreasing regularized maximum with error at most \(\varepsilon\), and
add one further \(\varepsilon\).  The result is \(W\) and satisfies
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}.  It is an exact product
generator.  Joint convexity follows from convex monotone composition.  At
the node, the derivatives of the regularized maximum with respect to its
inputs are branch-independent, so the sum over branches reduces to the
exact balance of each \(s_j\).  Only finitely many branches are active, and
the finitely many scalar profiles have one common terminal collar on each
full active branch.

Apply this construction to each \(H_n\).  Fix a summable positive sequence
\((\varepsilon_n)\), choose \(\widetilde H_n\) as in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-finite-activity-error}, and then choose
\(W_n\) as in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-smooth-majorant}.  Thus
\begin{equation}
                    H_n\leq W_n\leq H_n+6\varepsilon_n
                    \quad\text{on }\overline{U'}\times Q.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-row-error}
\end{equation}
Put
\[
             d_n=6\sum_{k>n}\varepsilon_k,\qquad G_n=W_n+d_n.
\]
Using \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-envelope-rows} and
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-row-error}, we obtain
\[
 G_{n+1}\leq H_{n+1}+6\varepsilon_{n+1}+d_{n+1}
       \leq H_n+d_n\leq W_n+d_n=G_n.
\]
Moreover \(G_n\to u\) pointwise.  This proves the first-stage assertion on
one fixed node neighbourhood, without a separate finite-centre case.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Full endpoints and ordinary branch points.}
At a full endpoint, work on a compact terminal product
\([-\infty,R]\times Q\), with \(R<0\), inside the given chart.  The metric
upper regularizations
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-upper-regularization}, followed by the
terminal insertion operator of
\Cref{lem:p071-terminal-polyhedral-insertion}, give finite continuous
jointly convex rows \(H_n\downarrow u\), nondecreasing in the branch
parameter and with exact endpoint trace.

For one such row, take the same partial Legendre profiles
\[
                 f(t,p)=\min_{y\in Q}(H(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y).
\]
Continuity on the closed polytope gives boundary-valid Fenchel--Moreau
reconstruction and finite dual sampling on a fixed smaller terminal core.
For each selected covector, the scalar endpoint theorem gives a smooth
convex nondecreasing profile, exactly constant on a terminal collar, within
\(\varepsilon\) of \(f(\,\cdot\,,p)\).  The lifted regularized-maximum
construction therefore gives \(W_n\) with
\[
                         H_n\leq W_n\leq H_n+5\varepsilon_n
\]
on one fixed terminal product neighbourhood.  The same summable-tail
calculation, with coefficient \(5\), makes the resulting
generators decrease to \(u\).

At an ordinary finite point of a branch there is no junction.  A smaller
chart is a relatively open convex subset of the polyhedron
\(\mathbf R\times P\), and the one-point case of the polyhedral convex
collapse gives a decreasing sequence of ambient smooth jointly convex
functions on one fixed smaller chart.

We have proved
\(\mathcal J_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}\) at every point.  Together with
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-easy-inclusion} and the tautological
inclusion
\(\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-polyhedral-collapse} and all fixed-neighbourhood
assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
The smaller neighbourhood depends only on the two nested geometric cores,

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The comparison class is decreasing-sequentially closed.}
The definition of $\mathcal C_X$ is local.  Restriction is immediate, and
gluing follows from the sheaf property of $\mathcal J_T$ after shrinking

$\mathcal C_X$: after a clopen shrinking it is independent of $z$, so one
takes $Y$ to be a point.

Let $u_n\downarrow u$ on an open $W\subset X$, with
$u_n\in\mathcal C_X(W)$, and first fix a node point
$(z_0,\eta,y_0)\in W$.  Choose a compact clopen neighbourhood
$C\ni z_0$, a standard star neighbourhood $U_0$, and a compact convex
polytope $Q$ containing $y_0$ in a relatively open convex neighbourhood,
so that
\[
                         C\times U_0\times Q\subset W.
\]
After shrinking only the finitely many exceptional collars, choose a
compact closed standard core $D\subset U_0$.

For fixed $n$, compactness of $C\times\{\eta\}\times Q$ gives finitely
many node factorization charts for $u_n$.  Intersect their standard star
neighbourhoods, refine their polyhedral neighbourhoods over a finite cover

sets, their common countable activity sets, and the exceptional set of
$U_0$.  Then $K_n$ is countable and
\begin{equation}
 u_n(z,p_b(t),y)=u_n(z,\eta,y)

 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-limit-inactive}
\end{equation}

$C\times Q$ supplies finitely many further factorization charts.  Together
with the node charts, these form a countable family describing $u_n$ on
$C\times D\times Q$.

Choose a countable clopen base in every metrizable quotient appearing in
these charts, for all $n$, and let $\mathcal B$ be the Boolean algebra of
clopen subsets of $C$ generated by their inverse images and by the domains
of the charts.  It is countable.  The evaluation map
\begin{equation}
 q:C\longrightarrow
 Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-common-quotient}
\end{equation}
is a continuous surjection onto a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
space.  The chosen bases separate points in every original quotient, so
each $u_n$, and hence $u$, is constant on the fibres of
$q\times\operatorname{id}_{D\times Q}$.

Write $u_n=\bar u_n\circ(q\times\operatorname{id})$.  Every
$\bar u_n$ is upper semicontinuous.  Indeed, if
$\bar u_n(\zeta,x)<s$, compactness of the fibre $q^{-1}(\zeta)$ gives a
finite product-neighbourhood cover inside $\{u_n<s\}$, and closedness of
the compact-to-Hausdorff quotient $q$ gives a product neighbourhood of
$(\zeta,x)$ inside $\{\bar u_n<s\}$.  The same holds for
$\bar u=\inf_n\bar u_n$, since
$\{\bar u<s\}=\bigcup_n\{\bar u_n<s\}$.

Every fibre $\bar u_n(\zeta,\cdot)$ belongs to $\mathcal J_T$.
Decreasing closure of that sheaf gives the same for
$\bar u(\zeta,\cdot)$.  Moreover
\[
                              K=\bigcup_{n\geq1}K_n
\]
is countable, and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-limit-inactive} passes to the
limit.  Thus $u\in\mathcal C_X$ near the node.  At an ordinary branch
point or a full endpoint, the same Boolean-algebra construction uses one
compact branch--polytope core and no activity set.  Hence
$\mathcal C_X$ is decreasing-sequentially closed, and minimality gives
\begin{equation}
                          \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal C_X.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-minimality}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Regularization on a fixed node neighbourhood.}
Let $u\in\mathcal C_X$ near $(z_0,\eta,y_0)$ and use a factorization as in
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-factorization} on
$C\times U\times V_0$, with finite exceptional set $A$ and common
countable activity set $K$.  Shrink the exceptional collars once and choose
a compact closed standard core $D\subset U$.  Choose a compact convex
polytope $Q\subset V_0$ and a relatively open convex neighbourhood
$V'\ni y_0$ with $\overline{V'}^{\,P}\subset Q$.  Fix a smaller standard
neighbourhood $U'$ whose closure lies in the interior of $D$.  All
subsequent approximants will be defined on the single product
$C\times U'\times V'$.

Collapse every full branch outside $A\cup K$ to the node.  The resulting
compact exact-star core $D_K$ is metrizable, and $\bar u$ factors through
$Y\times D_K\times Q$.  Give this compact product a compatible metric
$d$.  For $k\geq1$, put
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_k(\xi)=\max_{\omega\in Y\times D_K\times Q}
       \bigl(\max\{\bar u(\omega),-k\}-k\,d(\xi,\omega)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-upper-regularization}
\end{equation}
Then $\Phi_k$ is finite and continuous and
\begin{equation}
          \Phi_{k+1}\leq\Phi_k,
   \qquad \Phi_k\geq\bar u,
   \qquad \Phi_k\downarrow\bar u.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-upper-limit}
\end{equation}

For $\zeta\in Y$, apply the exact comparison envelope only in the
$D_K\times Q$ variables:
\begin{equation}
 c_k(\zeta,\cdot)
    =C^{\mathrm{ex}}\bigl(\Phi_k(\zeta,\cdot)\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-fibre-envelope}
\end{equation}
The envelope lemma and the insertion lemma give
\begin{equation}
 \bar u\leq c_k\leq\Phi_k,
 \qquad c_{k+1}\leq c_k,
 \qquad c_k\downarrow\bar u.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-envelope-limit}
\end{equation}
The nonexpanding estimate for $C^{\mathrm{ex}}$ and the uniform continuity
of $\Phi_k$ show that $c_k$ is jointly continuous on
$Y\times D_K\times Q$.

Choose nested finite clopen partitions $\mathscr Q_k$ of $Y$ whose meshes
tend to zero.  For $R\in\mathscr Q_k$, define
\begin{equation}
 a_{k,R}(x)=\max_{\zeta\in R}c_k(\zeta,x),
 \qquad
 a_k(\zeta,x)=a_{k,R_k(\zeta)}(x).
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-clopen-max}
\end{equation}

exact endpoint trace survives because the family is jointly continuous on
the compact terminal prism.  Lift $a_{k,R}$ to $D\times Q$ by making every
branch outside $A\cup K$ equal to its node slice; the two-stage barycentre
calculation in
\Cref{lem:p071-arbitrary-exact-star-polyhedral-insertion} shows that the
lift is still an exact comparison function.  Refinement and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-envelope-limit} give
\begin{equation}
                              a_{k+1}\leq a_k,
                 \qquad      a_k\downarrow\bar u.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-clopen-limit}
\end{equation}
For the upper limit, choose a maximizing point in $R_k(\zeta)$ and use its
convergence to $\zeta$ together with
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-upper-limit}; this also covers
the value $-\infty$.

Fix positive numbers $\varepsilon_k$ with
$\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty$.  For every $k$, apply
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-one-step} to the finite family
$\{a_{k,R}:R\in\mathscr Q_k\}$.  On the one fixed domain
$U'\times V'$ this gives generators $g_{k,R}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
                   a_{k,R}\leq g_{k,R}
                       \leq a_{k,R}+6\varepsilon_k.
 \label{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-family-smoothing}
\end{equation}
Define
\[
 w_k(z,x)=g_{k,R}(x)
 \quad\text{when }q(z)\in R\in\mathscr Q_k.
\]
The inverse images $q^{-1}(R)$ form a finite clopen partition of $C$, so
$w_k\in\mathcal G_{X,0}(C\times U'\times V')$.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-clopen-limit} and
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-family-smoothing} give
\[
                         w_{k+1}\leq w_k+6\varepsilon_{k+1}.
\]
Set
\[
             \tau_k=6\sum_{j>k}\varepsilon_j,
             \qquad G_k=w_k+\tau_k.
\]
Then $G_{k+1}\leq G_k$ and
$G_k\downarrow u$ on $C\times U'\times V'$.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The remaining strata.}
At a full endpoint, use a compact terminal branch--polytope core.  The
terminal insertion operator and the partial-Legendre smoothing in the
proof of \Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-polyhedral-collapse} give the same
nonexpanding fibre envelope and a uniform one-step estimate, now with
constant $5$.  Repeating the compact-metric regularization, finite clopen
partition, and summable-tail argument above gives one decreasing generator
sequence on a fixed terminal product neighbourhood.  At an ordinary point
of a branch, a smaller branch--polytope chart is one convex polyhedral
model, so \Cref{thm:p071-stone-polyhedral-collapse} gives the required
fixed-neighbourhood sequence directly.

We have proved $\mathcal C_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}$ at every point.
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-minimality} and the
tautological inclusion $\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X$, this
proves \eqref{eq:p071-stone-infinite-polyhedral-collapse} and the stated
fixed-neighbourhood assertion.
\end{proof}

\[

compact Stone parameter and of the polyhedral variable.  The transported
set therefore has the asserted uniformity on the developed chart.

On each chart, the transported comparison sheaf equals the intrinsic full
generated sheaf just identified.  Hence two chartwise definitions agree on
their overlap, so they glue to a well-defined sheaf $\mathcal C_X$, and the
three displayed sheaves coincide.  The proof uses one chart at a time and
no finite subdivision of it.  It therefore requires neither local
finiteness nor a bound on the number of cells meeting the chosen
neighbourhood.
\end{proof}
